findings.title: A refresh whose response is lost after the server rotated the token unpairs the paired device as refresh-token theft
findings.mechanism: refresh() persists the rotated refresh token only from the response body. On any non-401 failure it rethrows and deliberately keeps the OLD refresh token (line 135-136: "Offline or server trouble: keep the refresh token so the device reconnects later"). But POST /v1/child/refresh commits the rotation inside one transaction (apps/api/src/routes/child-auth.ts:230-231: issueRefreshToken + `set used_at = ...`), so if the response is lost after that commit — the client's own 20s DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS in packages/contracts/src/client.ts, a wifi/cellular switch, a Worker evicted after commit — the device keeps a token the server has already marked used_at. The next refresh presents it and hits the theft branch (child-auth.ts:205-213), which revokes the whole child_session, writes audit action 'child_session.revoked_token_reuse', and answers 401. The client's own 401 handler then calls forget() -> unpairChildDevice(), deleting the refresh token and profile. The comment's stated reasoning is wrong for exactly this interleaving: keeping the old token does not let the device reconnect later, it guarantees the pairing is destroyed. Refresh happens ~4x/hour per tablet, so one dropped response on a flaky home network ends the pairing.
findings.repro: Pair, let the access token lapse, make one child call whose /v1/child/refresh request reaches the server (rotation commits) but whose response never arrives (NETWORK), then make one more child call on a good connection.
findings.proof: PROBE B in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-claudecampsophie/b1b9c04d-3d1c-58be-b925-a948687d722a/scratchpad/hardening/hunt-r4/mobile-child/probes.probe.ts drives the real createChildSession against a mock that mirrors child-auth.ts. Printed: server log ['pair','refresh:committed_then_response_lost','refresh:THEFT_REVOKED','data:401 /v1/child/me'], sessionRevoked true, 'PROBE B still paired? false', and STORAGE_KEYS.childRefreshToken gone from storage. So the child is told "Ask a grown-up to connect this device again" and a parent has to mint a new pairing code, over one lost HTTP response.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the server a short reuse grace instead of treating every re-presentation as theft: private.child_refresh_tokens already has replaced_by, so in the `row.used_at` branch, when used_at is within a small window (e.g. 60s) and the replacement token has not itself been used, re-issue the access token for that replacement (returning the same replaced_by token) rather than revoking the session; revoke only outside the grace or when the replacement was already consumed. Optionally also record 'rotation in flight' on the device so the client can tell a lost rotation from a genuinely dead session.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: The child's rewards and help/report screens get no token retry, so the MOB-R2-02 recovery is missing on the surface that carries safety reports
findings.mechanism: withChildTokenRetry was applied to only two of the four child clients: apps/mobile/src/family/runtime.ts:45 and apps/mobile/src/homework/child-api.ts:18. The child's rewards screen (apps/mobile/app/(child)/rewards.tsx:44) and the child's help/report screen (apps/mobile/app/(child)/help.tsx:29) build `createMobileApi(tokenSource)` straight from the source registered in apps/mobile/src/lib/app-session.ts:51-52, which is `childSession.accessToken` with no wrapper. When the device clock moves backwards after a token was received — the exact state MOB-R2-02 was written for, where the cached token is dead server-side but the device still believes it live — these screens get 401 and nothing invalidates the cached token, so EVERY subsequent tap presents the same dead token. help.tsx maps UNAUTHENTICATED to CHILD_HELP_COPY.notConnected (apps/mobile/src/privacy/child-help.ts:88) and the report is not queued anywhere, so the child's attempt to report a problem is silently dropped while the homework screens in the same app recover on their first try. The screens stay broken for the whole remaining device-clock lifetime of the stale token (up to CHILD_ACCESS_TTL_SECONDS = 900s plus the backwards jump).
findings.repro: Pair; advance real time past the access-token lifetime; move the device clock back 30 minutes; tap a report choice on the child Help screen three times.
findings.proof: PROBE C in the scratch probe file. Printed: 'PROBE C bare attempt 1/2/3: UNAUTHENTICATED, refreshes=0' and server log ['pair','data:401 /v1/child/reports' x3,'data:401 /v1/child/me','refresh:ok','data:200 /v1/child/me'] — the bare client never triggers a refresh, the wrapped client recovers on its first call at the same instant.
findings.suggestedFix: Register the wrapped client, not the raw token source: have app-session.ts hand rewards/privacy a client (or a token source plus the retry) built once via withChildTokenRetry(createMobileApi(childSession.accessToken), childSession), or export the single wrapped childApi and have both screens use it, so the rule holds on every child surface rather than two of four.

findings.title: withChildTokenRetry gives the whole session one retry slot, not one per call: a second call refused at the same moment is told the device is not connected
findings.mechanism: `once` decides whether to retry by `session.invalidateAccessToken()`, which returns true only if a token was cached AT THAT MOMENT (child-session.ts:189-193). Two calls that both presented the same stale token race: the first 401 to land invalidates (true) and retries; the second finds `access === null`, gets false, and rethrows UNAUTHENTICATED even though the device is paired and the refresh that is already in flight would have served it. The predicate answers "is there a cached token" when the question is "did the call I just made present a token that is no longer current". Reachable without any explicit Promise.all: an in-flight request from a screen the child just navigated away from still resolves into `once` (apps/mobile/app/(child)/results.tsx:47-56 only sets `active=false`, the request keeps running), so the scan list's 401 can consume the slot and the scan-detail request the child is looking at fails; likewise the limits GET issued on scan-screen mount (apps/mobile/app/(child)/scan.tsx:99, failure swallowed) can consume it and make the child's POST /v1/assignments fail with "Ask a grown-up to connect this device again", so the scan is not sent.
findings.repro: Pair; advance past the token lifetime; move the device clock back 30 minutes; issue two child calls concurrently through childApi.
findings.proof: PROBE A in the scratch probe file. Printed: statuses ['fulfilled','rejected'], reasons ['ok','connect again'], server log ['pair','data:401 /v1/child/me','data:401 /v1/child/assignments','refresh:ok','data:200 /v1/child/me'] — one call recovered, the other was told the device is not connected while isPaired() was still true.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the retry decision per call rather than per session: have the wrapper capture the token it presented (e.g. accessToken() returns it, or invalidateAccessToken(presented) only clears when it matches) and retry once whenever the failed call presented a token AND the cached token is now different-or-absent. The existing single-flight refresher already collapses the concurrent refreshes, so both calls then get the fresh token and only one /v1/child/refresh is made.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: The parent's device list still says "Connected" for a child device whose session ended any way except logout or a parent action
findings.mechanism: The round-3 fix (API-AUTH-R2-05) stamps child_devices.revoked_at only in the logout handler (child-auth.ts:259-267). The parent's list derives connectedness purely from that column — GET /v1/family/devices selects only child_devices rows (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:429) and apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.ts:130 renders `d.revokedAt ? 'Disconnected' : 'Connected'` — so every other way a session ends leaves the tablet listed as Connected for good. Two such paths remain: (a) the refresh-token-reuse revocation at child-auth.ts:207, which HUNT4-MOB-1 shows is reachable from an ordinary lost response, and (b) natural expiry, since app.current_child_id() requires `s.expires_at > now()` (supabase/migrations/0001_core_identity.sql:363) while nothing stamps the device when CHILD_REFRESH_TTL_SECONDS (30 days) elapses on an unused tablet. In both cases the child sees "Ask a grown-up to connect this device again" while the one screen the parent would check to find out reports the device as Connected, with a live "Disconnect" button and no hint that a new pairing code is what is needed. Deletion, archive, consent withdrawal and parent revoke all do stamp the device, so this is the one-surface-fixed shape rather than a missing feature.
findings.repro: Pair a device, trigger the reuse revocation (present a rotated refresh token twice, as PROBE B does), then GET /v1/family/devices as the parent: the row still has revokedAt null. Same for a session whose expires_at has passed.
findings.proof: Read of the three files above; PROBE B shows the reuse revocation firing from a plain network fault. child-auth.ts:207 updates child_sessions only — grep over apps/api/src for child_devices confirms the only writers are guardians.ts:726 (consent), family.ts:399/453 (archive, parent revoke), child-auth.ts:123 (insert) and child-auth.ts:260 (logout).
findings.suggestedFix: Either stamp child_devices in the reuse branch too (and when a session is found expired), or better, stop deriving "Connected" from child_devices alone: have GET /v1/family/devices report per-device session liveness (exists a child_session with revoked_at is null and expires_at > now()) and let family-view.ts say "Needs a new connect code" for a device whose sessions have all ended, so no future revoke path can silently lie to the parent again.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: cancelScan's 'too_late' answer is discarded, so a child who stops a scan the server already accepted is told it stopped and is set up to send it twice
findings.mechanism: upload.ts:276-290 computes three distinct outcomes for cancelScan ('cancelled' | 'nothing_to_cancel' | 'too_late', the last from BUSINESS_RULE INVALID_TRANSITION) precisely so the caller can tell the child the truth. Both call sites throw the value away: scan.tsx:126 (`void cancelScan(...).catch(() => undefined)`) and scan.tsx:275, where the abort path then unconditionally sets `upload = {kind:'error', message: 'Stopped. Your pages are still here.'}` and resets attemptRef to a fresh createKey/finalizeKey (scan.tsx:276). If the child taps "Stop sending" while the finalize request is in flight, `cancellable` turns the aborted response into ScanCancelledError (upload.ts:126-134) even though the server committed the finalize. The cancel that follows normally succeeds because 'queued' is in CANCELLABLE_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES, but once the scan job has moved it out of 'queued' the cancel is refused with INVALID_TRANSITION (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:1066-1073) and returns 'too_late'. The child is then told the scan was stopped when it is being checked and charged, and because the idempotency keys were rotated, "Try again" creates a SECOND assignment for the same homework — two jobs and two page-allowance charges against AC_CAPTURE_06's one-job-one-charge.
findings.repro: Child taps "Stop sending" during the POST /v1/assignments/{id}/finalize round trip, and the scan job picks the assignment up out of 'queued' before the cancel POST lands; then tap "Try again".
findings.proof: Read of apps/mobile/app/(child)/scan.tsx:272-286, apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.ts:255-290, apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:1060-1080 and packages/contracts/src/homework.ts:149-171 (CANCELLABLE excludes extracting/checking/verifying, FINALIZED includes queued). No test exercises the 'too_late' branch of either call site.
findings.suggestedFix: Branch on the cancelScan result in scan.tsx: on 'cancelled' keep the current copy and the fresh attempt; on 'too_late' keep the SAME attempt (so "Try again" re-creates with the same createKey and is reported as already sent via the FINALIZED_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES path) and tell the child the scan was already on its way, e.g. "That one was already sent — check My scans."
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: Locking the parent area on a paired child tablet leaves mode 'parent' and strands the device on the PIN screen; a relaunch shows the parent/child chooser instead of the child's space
findings.mechanism: The new lockParentAreaOnDevice (mode.ts:65-71) is now the action behind both Lock buttons (ui.tsx:LockParentAreaButton) and the backgrounding handler (app-session.ts:74-78). It does four things: forgetParentUnlock, clearAdultCaches, resetNavigationToUnlock, relockOnServer. It never looks at STORAGE_KEYS.childRefreshToken and never touches the persisted mode, so on a device that holds a child pairing it (a) navigates to /(parent)/unlock — modeEffects.resetNavigationToUnlock, runtime.ts:138-143, does router.dismissAll() (a POP_TO_TOP that the root stack's StackRouter serves, see expo-router 57 build/global-state/router.js:83-88 and canDismiss at :110-125) then router.replace, so the child-space route below is popped off and the unlock screen becomes the only route; the unlock screen (app/(parent)/unlock.tsx:138-215) has no 'Back to my space' control, and with one route in the (parent) stack the native header shows no back arrow while the root Stack has headerShown:false (app/_layout.tsx:15) — and (b) leaves pl.mode = 'parent', so entryRoute('parent', paired, …, null) returns null (src/lib/entry.ts:13) and the next cold start of the child's tablet shows the parent/child chooser, not the child space. That is exactly the MOB-R2-04 symptom the sign-out path was fixed for (mode.ts:168-185 writes 'child' and calls resetNavigationToChildHome when a pairing exists) and the MOB-R2-05 rule the child layout enforces (ui.tsx:useChildModeOnFocus). Of the three ways out of the parent area, only the new lock fails to restore child mode on a paired device.
findings.repro: Paired family tablet (pl.child.refresh set). Parent taps Grown-ups → PIN → parent home (pl.mode='parent'). Parent taps 'Lock parent area' (or just sends the app to the background, app-session.ts:68-79). Screen becomes 'Parent area / Enter your 6-digit parent PIN'. Child picks up the tablet: no on-screen way back to their space (iPad: only the edge-swipe, the very thing MOB-R1-07 says a child cannot rely on; Android Back on a single-route root stack exits the app). After the app is killed or relaunched, index.tsx reads mode 'parent' and shows the 'I'm a parent / Connect a child's device' chooser instead of the child home.
findings.proof: Scratch vitest (now at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-claudecampsophie/b1b9c04d-3d1c-58be-b925-a948687d722a/scratchpad/hardening/hunt-r4/mobile-lock/lock-paired-tablet.scratch.test.ts) driving the real mode.ts + entry.ts: after enterParentMode then lockParentAreaOnDevice on a storage that holds pl.child.refresh, effects.calls === ['clear','unlock','relock'] (no 'child-home'), currentMode(storage) === 'parent', entryRoute('parent',true,true,null) === null while entryRoute('child',true,true,null) === '/(child)/home'. Ran `npx vitest run … --reporter=default` → 1 passed. The file was then moved out of the repo; `git status --porcelain` is empty.

As a minimum, add a 'Back to my space' button to app/(parent)/unlock.tsx whenever a child pairing exists, so the lock cannot leave a child on a PIN field with no exit.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: The unlock screen silently deletes the parent's stored biometric PIN whenever the signed-in user id cannot be read (offline with an expired access token)
findings.mechanism: biometricOffer (src/family/unlock.ts:25-33) folds three different states into one value: a DIFFERENT parent, a PIN with no recorded owner, and 'nobody signed in' all return 'other_user' (line 31). runtime.ts:90-93 then treats 'other_user' as a reason to DESTROY the secret: clearBiometricPin() deletes the SecureStore PIN plus pl.parent.biometricEnabled and pl.parent.biometricOwner (runtime.ts:70-74). parentAuth.userId() (src/lib/parent-auth.ts:122-126) returns null whenever getSession() yields no session — not only when nobody is signed in. In @supabase/auth-js 2.116 __loadSession refreshes an expired access token and, when that refresh fails, returns {data:{session:null}, error} unless the access token is still inside its real expiry window (GoTrueClient.js:2568-2590). So an offline device whose access token has passed expires_at reports 'no signed-in parent', and the enrolment of the parent who is still signed in is deleted. Nothing is shown to the parent; the screen just stops offering Face ID, and re-enrolling is impossible until the device is online again because save() throws without a user id (runtime.ts:97-99).
findings.repro: Parent enables 'Use Face ID or fingerprint next time' (PIN stored, owner recorded). Later, in airplane mode and more than the access-token TTL (1h by default) after the last refresh, they open the app and tap Grown-ups. app/(parent)/unlock.tsx:63-65 runs biometricPinStore.isEnabled() on mount (the effect is declared above the `if (!api)` early return, so it runs even with no usable session) → userId() null → biometricOffer({enabled:true, ownerUserId:'user-a'}, null) === 'other_user' → clearBiometricPin(). The keychain PIN and both flags are gone for good; the parent types the PIN and, once online, has to re-enrol.
findings.proof: Code path read end to end; the deleting branch is the one the round's own test pins: apps/mobile/src/family/screens-r2.review.test.ts:98 asserts biometricOffer({enabled:true, ownerUserId:'user-a'}, null) === 'other_user'. supabase-js behaviour confirmed by reading node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+auth-js@2.116.0/node_modules/@supabase/auth-js/dist/main/GoTrueClient.js:2568-2590 ('const accessTokenStillValid = …; return this._returnResult({ data: { session: null }, error })'). No mobile test covers the runtime store, so nothing catches it.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the unknown case from the mismatch: return a third outcome ('unknown') for signedInUserId === null and have isEnabled() just return false for it — fail closed without deleting. Delete only when a different user id is actually signed in, plus the existing deletes on sign-out and account closure (runtime.ts:174). The legacy ownerUserId === null case can stay a delete if that migration cost is wanted.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: Signing out is hidden from a child on the unlock screen, but 'Turn off biometric unlock' is left beside the PIN field
findings.mechanism: unlock.tsx:204-212 hides 'Lock parent area' and 'Sign out' unless a live unlock brought the parent here, with the stated reason 'never beside the PIN field, where a child could reach them'. The 'Turn off biometric unlock' button (lines 188-198) is rendered on the same screen with no such gate: its only condition is canBiometric && biometricOn. It calls biometricPinStore.clear(), which deletes the keychain PIN and both flags — a destructive, parent-only setting change performed with no PIN, no OS prompt and no confirmation.
findings.repro: Paired tablet, parent has Face ID unlock enabled. Child taps 'Grown-ups' on the child home (app/(child)/home.tsx:108-113) → /(parent)/unlock. isEnabled() is true (same parent signed in), so the child sees 'Turn off biometric unlock' and taps it. The parent's enrolment is deleted; next time they must type the PIN and re-enable, with no indication of what happened.
findings.proof: Read of app/(parent)/unlock.tsx:163-212: the toggle and the 'Turn off' button sit inside the PIN <Card> with no `unlockActive` condition, while the Lock/Sign out block immediately below is wrapped in `{unlockActive ? … : null}`. biometricPinStore.clear() is clearBiometricPin (apps/mobile/src/family/runtime.ts:70-74, 115), which deletes the SecureStore entry unconditionally.
findings.suggestedFix: Put 'Turn off biometric unlock' behind the same `unlockActive` condition as Lock/Sign out (or behind the ParentalGate already used on this screen for the portal link), so no PIN-less visitor can change the parent's security settings.

findings.title: The client-side unlock is not forgotten when the Supabase session disappears, and mounted parent screens are never re-gated on that event
findings.mechanism: The auth watcher's signed-out branch (app-session.ts:61-65) clears the adult caches and unbinds the store SDK, but does not call forgetParentUnlock(), so parentUnlockedUntilMs keeps running for the rest of its window across an auth-state change. useParentAccess (ui.tsx:266-308) re-checks only on mount (:297) and on AppState 'active' (:304-305) — never on focus and never on the auth change — so a parent screen that was 'ready' keeps that state, keeps its already-loaded family data in component state, and keeps an ApiClient whose token source resolves the CURRENT session. A different parent who signs in on the device inside that window therefore reaches parent screens without the fresh PIN unlock the sign-in screen promises (app/(parent)/sign-in.tsx:19 'After signing in, the parent area still needs a fresh PIN unlock'), and sees the previous parent's rendered data until a reload swaps in their own.
findings.repro: Parent A unlocks the parent area on the device and has two parent screens in the stack, so /(parent)/home stays mounted in state 'ready'. A's session is ended elsewhere (portal 'sign out everywhere', or a password change) — onAuthStateChange fires, the watcher clears caches but the unlock window (300s by default, ADULT_UNLOCK_TTL_SECONDS) stays live. The top screen shows SignInPrompt; parent B signs in there; sign-in.tsx:61 replaces to /(parent)/unlock, where unlockActive is still true. Pressing the header back arrow returns to the still-mounted home screen, which is still 'ready': A's family data is on screen and any refresh fetches B's family — no PIN was entered.
findings.proof: Read of app-session.ts:55-66 (no forgetParentUnlock in the !signedIn branch; mode.ts exports it and only signOutParent/enterChildMode/lockParentAreaOnDevice call it) and ui.tsx:293-307 (the only re-check triggers are mount and AppState 'active'). parentAuth.tokenSource (src/lib/parent-auth.ts:129-133) reads the live session, so the captured client follows whoever is signed in now.
findings.suggestedFix: In the watcher's !signedIn branch call forgetParentUnlock() (and, ideally, have useParentAccess re-check on parentAuth.watch and on screen focus as well as on foreground), so an auth change closes the client-side grant instead of leaving it open for the next session.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: Account closure puts a paired device into child mode pointing at a family that has just been deleted, and leaves the child's refresh token and cached nickname on it
findings.mechanism: signOutClosedAccountOnDevice (runtime.ts:184-190) reuses signOutParentOnDevice and only noops the two navigation effects. signOutParent (src/lib/mode.ts:173-184) still writes pl.mode = 'child' whenever STORAGE_KEYS.childRefreshToken is present, and deliberately leaves the pairing and pl.child.profile alone. For an account closure that rule is wrong: an owner can only close their sign-in after the whole-family deletion (ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY.familyDeletionRequired, packages/contracts/src/account.ts:62), so the child's session is already revoked. The device is therefore left in child mode for a deleted family, with the child's refresh token and cached nickname still in the keychain, and index.tsx sends every launch straight to the child space because entryRoute('child', paired=true, …) returns '/(child)/home' (src/lib/entry.ts:13).
findings.repro: Family tablet paired to one child; parent deletes the family, then deletes their account from app/(parent)/privacy.tsx:143. privacy.tsx calls signOutClosedAccountOnDevice → mode 'child'. Relaunch: index.tsx → /(child)/home → childApi /v1/child/me answers UNAUTHENTICATED → 'not_connected' state (app/(child)/home.tsx:75-85), which offers only 'Enter a connect code' and no 'Grown-ups' button. The adult's route to a new sign-up/sign-in runs through /pair, which (because the stale token is still stored) shows 'This device is connected to <nickname>'s space' → 'Use a different code' → Back → welcome chooser. pl.child.profile still holds the deleted child's nickname.

The archive/family-deletion side is confirmed to revoke child_sessions and child_devices in apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:397-400 and supabase/migrations/0620_deletion_purge.sql.

Independently, give the child home's 'not_connected' state a grown-up route to /(parent)/unlock.

findings.title: The Children screen treats a whole-family deletion request as a per-child one: it names the wrong scope and removes controls the API still honours
findings.mechanism: children.tsx:139 reads child.deletionPending, and the server sets that flag for a FAMILY-scope request as well as a child-scope one (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:122-125: `and (d.scope = 'family' or d.target_child_id = c.id)`). The route-level rule is narrower: visibleChild (family.ts:50-58) excludes only requests with target_child_id = c.id (plus a family already tombstoned), so while a family-scope request is merely 'requested'/'processing' the API still accepts PATCH /v1/children/:id, activation and pairing — and /v1/children/:id/archive never consults visibleChild at all (family.ts:389-391). The screen meanwhile prints, for every child, 'You asked for <nickname>'s data to be deleted' (line 231) and removes Pair, Assign a slot, Edit profile and Archive (lines 237, 251, 261), so the parent is told they asked for something they did not ask for and is blocked from work the server would accept — including archiving, which is how the Plan screen tells them to free a paid slot (the slot is only released by the purge, supabase/migrations/0620_deletion_purge.sql:214).
findings.repro: Parent requests deletion of the WHOLE family from Privacy (scope 'family', status 'requested'). GET /v1/family now returns deletionPending true for every child. On the mobile Children screen each card shows 'Data deletion under way. You asked for <nickname>'s data to be deleted…' and offers no Edit/Pair/Assign/Archive, while POST /v1/children/<id>/archive and PATCH /v1/children/<id> would both succeed for those children.

findings.title: The 15-minute recovery grant is unreachable on the mobile-link path: an abandoned /update-password tab changes the account password with no proof, for ever
findings.mechanism: `const fromRecoveryLink = recovery.status === 'ready' || recoverySession?.recoveryActive() === true;` (line 92-93). `recovery` is component state written exactly once, by the effect at lines 48-65 whose `started.current` ref guarantees a single run, and nothing ever resets it back to 'none'. So for an implicit-flow (mobile-requested) recovery link the FIRST disjunct is permanently true while the tab is mounted, and the adapter-side bound is never consulted. That makes RECOVERY_GRANT_MS (supabase-auth.ts:142), `openRecovery`/`closeRecovery` (supabase-auth.ts:161-167, 266, 226) and `recoveryActive()` (supabase-auth.ts:251-253) dead on this path: `mustProve` (line 95) stays false, the 'Current password' Field (lines 143-157) is never rendered, and onSubmit (lines 110-124) goes straight to `account.updatePassword(password)`. supabase-auth.ts:138-141 claims the opposite in so many words: 'a sign-out closes it, so an abandoned tab is not a standing permission to take the account over'. The R2 acceptance test only drives the adapter (UpdatePasswordPage.reauth.test.tsx:294-320 asserts recoveryActive() flips false after 16 minutes) and never checks that the PAGE honours it, which is why the bypass survived.
findings.repro:
1. Parent requests a password reset inside the phone app (apps/mobile/src/lib/parent-auth.ts:93 sets redirectTo `<portal>/update-password`; that client has no flowType, i.e. implicit, and detectSessionInUrl:false), so the emailed link is `https://portal/update-password#access_token=…&refresh_token=…&type=recovery`.
2. They open it in a shared family/school/library browser. readRecoveryLinkTokens parses the hash, acceptRecoveryLink adopts the session and opens the 15-minute grant, and the page sets recovery={status:'ready'}.
3. They are interrupted and walk away, leaving the tab open (supabase-js keeps the session alive with persistSession+autoRefreshToken).
4. Twenty minutes — or three hours — later the next person at that keyboard types a new password in the still-open tab and presses 'Save password'. No current password is asked for, the change succeeds, and they own the parent account (and thereby every child's homework, verdicts, safety reports and guardian emails).
findings.proof: Scratch probe (labeled fake account, no network) run in the scratchpad worktree at 8bc022b, now at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-claudecampsophie/b1b9c04d-3d1c-58be-b925-a948687d722a/scratchpad/hardening/hunt-r4/web-auth/zzprobe-stale-recovery.test.tsx. It renders UpdatePasswordPage at `/update-password#access_token=…&type=recovery`, lets acceptRecoveryLink resolve (which sets the fake grant open), then flips the fake `recoveryActive()` to false to model the 15 minutes lapsing, and asserts: `screen.queryByLabelText('Current password')` is null, `verifyPassword` was never called, and `updatePassword` was called with 'attacker-chosen-pass'. Command: `cd <wt>/apps/web && npx vitest run --reporter=default src/pages/auth/zzprobe-stale-recovery.test.tsx` → '✓ 1 test (1 passed)'. Note the probe types into the New password field first, so the component re-renders with the lapsed grant and still shows no proof field — the bypass is not a stale-closure artefact.
findings.suggestedFix: Stop trusting the page's own `recovery` state as the grant. Compute `fromRecoveryLink` from the adapter only (`recoverySession?.recoveryActive() === true`), and have `acceptRecoveryLink` remain the thing that opens that bounded grant (it already does, supabase-auth.ts:266). For adapters without the capability the existing refusal at lines 96-105 already covers the fallback. Add a page-level regression test that advances the clock past RECOVERY_GRANT_MS on the implicit-hash path and expects the 'Current password' field to appear.
findings.leadDecision: Remove the `recovery.status === "ready" ||` disjunct. recoveryActive() is the ONE source of the grant, so the 15-minute bound and the single use apply to the mobile-link path too (acceptRecoveryLink already opens the grant). The failed-link notice keeps today behaviour.

findings.title: A sign-out that supabase-js refused is reported as success: the refresh token stays in localStorage while the portal navigates to /sign-in
findings.mechanism: `async signOut(scope = 'local') { closeRecovery(); await auth.signOut({ scope }); }` throws away the `{ error }` that supabase-js returns, and supabase-js does not reject. In @supabase/auth-js 2.116.0 `_signOut` (dist/module/GoTrueClient.js) starts with `_useSession`; when `__loadSession` finds the stored access token past EXPIRY_MARGIN it tries a refresh, and if that refresh fails at the fetch level with the access token genuinely expired it returns `{ data: { session: null }, error }`. `_signOut` then hits `if (sessionError && !isAuthSessionMissingError(sessionError)) return this._returnResult({ error: sessionError })` and returns BEFORE `removeCurrentSession()` — the session, including its refresh token, is left in localStorage and no /logout request is ever sent, so the refresh token is still valid server-side. SignOutControl.tsx:36-41 then does `try { await auth.signOut('local'); } finally { setBusy(false); void navigate('/sign-in', { replace: true }); }` — no catch, no check that `currentSession()` is now null, and the navigation happens unconditionally. Nothing on screen contradicts it: /sign-in is not a portal path (App.tsx:160) so the 'Signed in as p•••@…' line is not rendered there, and SignInPage.tsx never redirects a still-signed-in visitor — it just shows the sign-in form. This defeats exactly the threat SignOutControl.tsx:8-12 was written for ('On a shared family, school or library computer the next person could read the family's children, homework scans, verdicts, points, safety reports, devices and guardian emails, because read screens need no PIN').
findings.repro:
1. Parent signs in to the portal on a shared/library computer and leaves the tab idle for over an hour, so the stored access token is expired (the refresh token is still good).
2. The network drops (captive portal expired, wifi flap) or Supabase auth is unreachable at fetch level.
3. Parent clicks 'Sign out'. POST /v1/adult/lock fails and is swallowed (lines 31-35, by design). `auth.signOut('local')` resolves after ~25 s of retries WITHOUT clearing storage, the button stops saying 'Signing out…', and the browser lands on /sign-in showing an empty sign-in form. The parent leaves.
4. Network returns. The next person at that browser types /app: supabase-js recovers the session from localStorage, refreshes the token, `currentSession()` returns the parent's session and RequireParent renders the family's data.
findings.proof: Scratch probe at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-claudecampsophie/b1b9c04d-3d1c-58be-b925-a948687d722a/scratchpad/hardening/hunt-r4/web-auth/zzprobe-signout-offline.test.ts — a REAL @supabase/supabase-js client built through createSupabaseAuth's factory with an injected always-rejecting fetch, an expired session seeded into jsdom localStorage under 'sb-example-auth-token', then `await auth.signOut('local')`. Command: `cd <wt>/apps/web && npx vitest run --reporter=default src/lib/zzprobe-signout-offline.test.ts` → '✓ 1 test (1 passed)', stdout: `PROBE stored session after signOut: {"access_token":"synthetic.expired.jwt","refresh_token":"synthetic-refresh-token",…}` and `PROBE fetch attempts: 8`. The adapter's signOut resolved without throwing, so SignOutControl's finally navigated to /sign-in. (Checked the other failure shapes too: with a still-valid access token, or a 4xx/5xx from /logout, 2.116.0 DOES call removeCurrentSession before returning the error, so those paths are safe — this is the one hole.)
findings.suggestedFix: Make the adapter surface the outcome: `const { error } = await auth.signOut({ scope }); if (error) throw error;` (or return a boolean), and in SignOutControl replace the bare `try/finally` with an error path — on failure re-check `auth.currentSession()`, and if a session is still there keep the parent on the page with a plain refusal ('We could not end your session — you are still signed in. Try again when you are back online') instead of navigating to /sign-in. Belt and braces: after a successful sign-out assert `currentSession() === null` before navigating. Regression test: the App.signout.test.tsx fake should have a case where `signOut` leaves `current` non-null and assert the router stays on /app and a refusal is shown.
findings.leadDecision: A refused sign-out is not success: report it and do not leave the page as if signed out while the refresh token is still stored. Clearing this browser storage explicitly is acceptable; silently navigating is not.

findings.title: Archiving a child is one-way in every client, while the new confirmation promises "You can activate them again later"
findings.mechanism: The new archive flow (ChildrenPage.tsx:318-345) tells the parent "You can activate them again later while a paid slot is free." POST /v1/children/:id/archive then sets status='archived'. But the card's control chain renders nothing for an archived child: the status branch falls through to `null` (line 304 — only 'active' and 'draft' have branches) and the Edit/Archive row is suppressed by `child.status === 'archived' || deletionPending ? null :` (line 305). The activate button exists only inside the `child.status === 'draft'` branch (lines 285-295). Mobile is the same: apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.ts:77 sets `canActivate: draft && unused > 0`. So no surface can call the activate route for an archived child even though the API allows it — apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:334-376 only short-circuits status 'active' and has no draft-only guard, and it clears `archived_at = null` on success. The archive signed the child's devices out, so the family loses that child's access with no in-product way back.
findings.repro: Family with 2 paid slots and one active child Riley. Children page → "Archive (keeps history, frees the slot)" → "Yes, archive Riley". Riley's card now shows only "Status: Archived: history only" and zero buttons; no other portal or mobile screen offers activation.
findings.proof: Scratch vitest probe (<scratchpad>/hardening/hunt-r4/web-portal/children-probe.test.tsx) rendering ChildrenPage with one archived child and paidSlots 2 printed: `buttons on an archived child card: []` and `archived card text: "RileyGrade 3 · ages 8-10Status: Archived: history only"`. `grep -rn "activate" apps/web/src apps/mobile/src apps/mobile/app` shows the only family-side caller is ChildrenPage.tsx:291 inside the draft branch, and family-view.ts:77 gates mobile on `draft &&`.
findings.suggestedFix: Render an "Activate again" control on an archived card when `unusedSlots > 0` (reusing `activate()`, which the API already supports for an archived profile), with the same no-purchase copy as the draft branch and an honest note when no slot is free. Mirror it in apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.ts (`canActivate: (draft || archived) && unused > 0`). If re-activation is deliberately not offered, delete the promise from the confirmation text instead.
findings.leadDecision: Add activation to the archived card on both clients (POST /children/:childId/activate exists), so the confirmation promise is true. If a step-up is refused, keep the card usable.

findings.title: The deletion-pending notice tells the parent to cancel the request on the privacy page; no cancel exists anywhere
findings.mechanism: The new `deletionPending` notice (ChildrenPage.tsx:261-268) reads: "You asked for {nickname}'s data to be deleted, so nothing can be changed, paired or activated for them. Cancel the request on the privacy page if you did not mean it." There is no cancel: apps/api/src/routes/privacy.ts exposes only `r.post('/deletion')` and `r.get('/deletion')` (no PATCH/DELETE, no /cancel), no code path anywhere sets `deletion_requests.status = 'cancelled'`, and PrivacyControlsPage's "Deletion requests" list (lines 806-822) renders status text only, with no control. The same privacy page says the opposite two sections earlier: "Deleting stops processing immediately … This can't be undone." So the round's new screen promises reversibility for the product's most destructive, irreversible action and sends the parent to a page that contradicts it.
findings.repro: Request deletion of one child's data on /app/privacy (typed confirmation + PIN). Go to /app/children: the card shows the notice with a link to /app/privacy. Follow it: nothing there can cancel, and the page says the deletion cannot be undone.
findings.proof: `grep -n "r\\.(post|patch|delete)(" apps/api/src/routes/privacy.ts` → only /deletion (POST), /exports, /exports/answer-key, /safety-reports, /child/reports, /admin/safety-reports. `grep -rn "deletion_requests" apps/ packages/ | grep cancelled` → no hits; `grep -rn cancelled supabase/migrations/*.sql | grep -i deletion` matches only the promo state machine and the jobs table. `grep -n cancel apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.tsx` shows no cancel control. docs/Deployment_Runbook.md:414 mentions FAMILY_ACTIVE "the deletion was cancelled" as a hypothetical with no implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Change the notice to what is true — the request cannot be cancelled, deletion completes by <completeBy>, contact support if it was a mistake — or implement a cancel endpoint plus a control on the privacy page (a `requested`-only transition to 'cancelled' that also cancels the deletion_purge job) before making that promise.
findings.leadDecision: Correct the copy. There is NO cancel-deletion endpoint and none is being added this round (the spec does not require one): say the deletion is under way, that the child stays listed and unusable until the purge, and that stopping it needs support. Do not invent a control.

findings.title: The child PATCH form always sends all three fields, so it silently reverts the other guardian's grade change — the opposite of what its own comment claims
findings.mechanism: EditChildForm's doc comment (ChildrenPage.tsx:392-395) says "Only the fields the parent changed are sent, so a concurrent edit by the other guardian is not overwritten wholesale." The code does the opposite: `submit` always builds `{ nickname, gradeLevel, ageBand }` from its initial-state-seeded inputs (lines 422-426) and sends all three. The API applies every present field (`coalesce(${body.gradeLevel ?? null}::int, grade_level)` in apps/api/src/routes/family.ts). So guardian A opens the edit form while the child is in grade 3, guardian B saves grade 4, then A corrects only the nickname → the grade goes back to 3 with no warning. The grade is what practice generation is pitched at, which is the harm WEB-R2-03 set out to fix. EditFamilyForm (FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:170-178) has the same shape for displayName/timezone.
findings.repro: Two tabs (or two guardians) on /app/children with Riley in grade 3. Tab 2: Edit profile → grade 4 → save. Tab 1 (still showing grade 3): Edit profile → change only the nickname → save. The PATCH body carries gradeLevel 3 and the API writes it, dropping the grade bump.
findings.proof: Scratch probe (children-probe.test.tsx, nickname-only edit) printed: `PATCH body for a nickname-only edit: {"nickname":"Riley R.","gradeLevel":3,"ageBand":"8-10"}`. The repo's own new test agrees: ChildrenPage.profile.test.tsx:92-96 expects `body: { nickname: 'Riley R.', gradeLevel: 4, ageBand: '8-10' }` although the age band was never touched.
findings.suggestedFix: Build the body from a diff against the props the form was seeded with (omit each field equal to `child.<field>`) and keep the submit button disabled when nothing changed — the contract's refine already rejects an empty body. Same for EditFamilyForm. If wholesale writes are wanted, add an optimistic-concurrency token and correct the comment.
findings.leadDecision: Send only the fields the parent changed, so a save cannot revert another guardian edit. The comment already claims this; make it true.

findings.title: A successful family name/time-zone save shows no confirmation, and a failed reload after it leaves the old name plus an error banner on screen
findings.mechanism: EditFamilyForm owns its own `useAction()` and renders `<ActionFeedback ... stepUpAction="Saving your family details" />` inside the form (line 223). On success it calls `onSaved()` (line 179), which does `setEditing(false)` then `onChanged()` (lines 105-108) — unmounting the form and with it the only place the "Saved. Your family is …" message could appear. The screen's only evidence of the save is the reloaded /v1/family; when that reload fails, `useLastGood` (SecurityPage.tsx:~158) keeps the previous overview, so the page shows the OLD name and OLD time zone plus an ErrorState. The parent concludes the save failed and retries, while the server has already changed the zone every daily release, weekly review and school report is planned in. ChildrenPage gets this right (its feedback lives in ChildCard, outside the form), so this screen is out of step with the codebase's own documented pattern ("forms and success messages are not unmounted by a refresh").
findings.repro: On /app: Edit family name and time zone → set name "The Riveras" → Save family details, with the following GET /v1/family failing (offline blip). The heading still reads the old name, no success text appears, and "Network request failed / Try again" is shown.
findings.proof: Scratch test (<scratchpad>/hardening/hunt-r4/web-portal/family-save.test.tsx) with a fake API whose PATCH succeeds and whose second GET /v1/family rejects with NETWORK printed: `role=status nodes after save: []`, `h2s now: [ 'Test Family', 'Parental consent', 'Manage' ]`, `body mentions Europe/Berlin? false`, `body mentions Saved.? false`, `error banner text: [ 'Network request failedTry again' ]`.
findings.suggestedFix: Lift the action state (or at least the outcome) into FamilySummary and render ActionFeedback outside the collapsible form, as ChildCard does — keep `feedback` in FamilySummary, pass `run` down, and close the form only once the message is mounted where it survives.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: PIN reset drops an owner's aal2 session whenever the factor lookup is slower than the parent's password submit
findings.mechanism: WEB-R2-08 adds a two-step re-verification step, but it is gated on state filled by an unawaited effect: `useEffect` calls `account.assuranceLevel()` and `account.verifiedTotpFactorId()` and only then sets `twoStepFactorId` (PinResetPage.tsx:24-37). The password form reads that state at submit time — `if (outcome.ok) setStep(twoStepFactorId ? 'two_step' : 'pin')` (line 60). `verifiedTotpFactorId()` is a network call (supabase-auth.ts:288, `auth.mfa.listFactors()`). If it has not resolved when the parent submits (autofill + Enter, slow network, or a transient failure taking the `() => undefined` rejection branch), the flow goes straight to the PIN step, the password grant's new aal1 session replaces the aal2 one, the warning paragraph is never shown, and the two-step form is never rendered afterwards (the effect's only dep is `account`, and `step` is already 'pin'). Every /admin page then refuses with "Owner administration requires an MFA session" — exactly the failure this change was written to prevent.
findings.repro: Owner at aal2 opens /app/security/reset-pin and submits the autofilled password before listFactors returns.
findings.proof: Scratch test (<scratchpad>/hardening/hunt-r4/web-portal/pin-reset-race.test.tsx) with `verifiedTotpFactorId()` returning a promise released only after the password click and `assuranceLevel()` = 'aal2' printed: `reached PIN step without two-step? true`, `two-step field present? false`, `PIN reset sent? 1`, `verifyTotp calls: 0`.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the check a resolved precondition rather than a race: hold the lookup in a three-state value ('checking' | factorId | null), disable or relabel "Confirm it's you" while it is 'checking', and re-run the decision after the sign-in (or await the lookup inside onSubmit before signInWithPassword). Handle the rejection branch explicitly instead of silently treating it as "no two-step".
findings.leadDecision: The owner aal2 path must not depend on a race: block the password submit until the assurance/factor lookup has settled, or read it before offering the form.

findings.title: The shared step-up prompt lost the live region the old notices had, so a refusal on a long form is announced nowhere and rendered off-screen
findings.mechanism: Every step-up notice replaced this round was `<div className="notice" role="alert">` (old SecurityPage.StepUpNotice, HomeworkPage.StepUpNotice, RewardsPage.ActionFeedback, learning feedback.tsx — all visible in the diff). The shared replacement is a plain `<fieldset className="notice">` (StepUpPrompt.tsx:98-156) with no role, no aria-live and no focus move; only the wrong-PIN line (146) and the post-unlock status (92) are live. Every other refusal on the same screens still goes through ErrorState, which is `role="alert"` (components/states.tsx:14). Concretely: on the learning planner, ActionFeedback sits at ScheduleSection.tsx:169 while the submit button is at line 319 — about 150 lines of fields apart — so a parent who presses "Save schedule" with a stale unlock gets a PIN field far above the viewport, nothing announced, no focus moved, and no visible change near the button they pressed.
findings.repro: On /app/learning, let the unlock lapse, fill in the schedule, scroll to the bottom and press Save. The API answers STEP_UP_REQUIRED; the page appears to do nothing and a screen reader says nothing.
findings.proof: Scratch test (<scratchpad>/hardening/hunt-r4/web-portal/stepup-live.test.tsx) rendering learning ActionFeedback with a STEP_UP_REQUIRED error printed `STEP_UP alerts: [] statuses: []`, while the same component with RATE_LIMITED printed one alert. `grep -n "role=|aria-live|autoFocus|focus()" apps/web/src/components/StepUpPrompt.tsx` shows only lines 92 and 146.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the prompt container `role="alert"` (or wrap the legend/explanation in an aria-live="assertive" region) and move focus to the PIN input on mount via a ref effect, the way useFocusOnNavigation already does for headings. Rendering it adjacent to the pressed control would also close the off-screen case.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: The privacy page still claims PencilLift "emails the guardians on this account" — the exact overclaim CS-R2-06 removed from the contract copy this round
findings.mechanism: CS-R2-06 rewrote PARENT_SAFETY_FLAG_COPY.emailSent (packages/contracts/src/privacy.ts:225-234) precisely because "emailed the guardians on this account" was untrue: the job emails only verified addresses and stamps `sent` as soon as ONE accepts (apps/api/src/jobs/dispatcher.ts:365-410 — `addresses = recipients.flatMap(r => r.email && r.email_verified ? [r.email] : [])`, `if (accepted === 0) … else set parent_email_status = 'sent'`, with `refused > 0` logged as PARTIAL). The per-flag line on the page now uses the corrected constant, but the section's own intro paragraph two lines above still hard-codes the removed claim: "… and emails the guardians on this account so they know to look". An unverified co-guardian, or one whose address bounced, reads on the same screen that they were emailed. Worse, the wrong copy is now pinned by a test (PrivacyControlsPage.test.tsx:750 asserts /emails the guardians on this account/i) while apps/api/tests/jobs-r2.review.test.ts:467 asserts the contract string must NOT say it. apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.ts:336 carries the same sentence.
findings.repro: A family with an owner (verified address) and a co-guardian whose email is unverified. A safety flag is filed; the email goes only to the owner and the report is stamped `sent`. The co-guardian opens /app/privacy → Safety reports: the intro says PencilLift "emails the guardians on this account", although nothing was sent to them.
findings.proof: `grep -rn "emails the guardians|emailed the guardians" apps/ packages/` → PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:1081 and apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.ts:336 still say it; PrivacyControlsPage.test.tsx:750 and parent-privacy.test.ts:375 pin it; jobs-r2.review.test.ts:467 asserts the contract copy must not. Read of dispatcher.ts:365-410 confirms verified-only recipients and one-acceptance `sent`.
findings.suggestedFix: Rewrite the intro paragraph to match the corrected constant — "… and emails at least one verified guardian address so a grown-up knows to look; an unverified address, or one the provider refused, is not reached" — or drop the claim from the intro and let each flag's own line (which already uses PARENT_SAFETY_FLAG_COPY) carry it. Update the two tests that pin the old wording and apply the same change to the mobile string.
findings.leadDecision: Remove the overclaim and render the settled contract copy (PARENT_SAFETY_FLAG_COPY), which CS-R2-06 already corrected.

findings.title: An expired download link shows "That download link expired" and "Your download link is ready." at the same time
findings.mechanism: `fetchLink` stores the success outcome "Your download link is ready." in `action.outcome` and sets `link`. The expiry timer then sets `link = null` and `expired = true` (lines 611-624). Render order is: the expired paragraph (644-647), then `{link ? null : <ActionOutcome outcome={action.outcome} … />}` (656) — with `link` now null, the stale success message renders again. The parent sees two contradicting `role="status"` lines and a screen reader reads both.
findings.repro: On /app/privacy with a ready export: press "Get download link", wait 60 s.
findings.proof: Scratch copy of the repo's own WEB-R2-07 test with one added probe (<scratchpad>/hardening/hunt-r4/web-portal/export-stale.test.tsx) printed after advancing the pinned clock past expiry: `STATUSES AFTER EXPIRY: ["That download link expired for your safety. Ask for a new one to download the file.","Your download link is ready."]`.
findings.suggestedFix: Clear the outcome when the link expires (`action.setOutcome(null)` inside the timer's `done()`), or suppress ActionOutcome's success branch while `expired` is true so only the expiry line speaks.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: The download link's expiry is the server's instant compared against the browser clock, so a skewed clock keeps a dead link clickable
findings.mechanism: `const remaining = new Date(link.expiresAt).getTime() - Date.now();` mixes two clocks: `expiresAt` is stamped by the API/storage signer, `Date.now()` is the device's. The comment above it claims "the page can never offer a URL that would answer with the storage service's error document", but a device clock five minutes behind gives remaining ≈ 360 s, so the "Download file" anchor stays on screen and clickable for five minutes after the signature died — exactly the outcome WEB-R2-07 was written to prevent. A clock ahead of the server drops a perfectly valid link immediately.
findings.repro: Set the device clock 5 minutes slow, request a link, wait 90 s, click "Download file" → the storage provider's error document, while the page still says "link valid until …".
findings.proof: Read of PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:605-624 against apps/api/src/routes/export-download.ts (DOWNLOAD_URL_SECONDS = 60, `expiresAt` derived from the server clock); there is no clamp and no local-elapsed measurement anywhere in the component.
findings.suggestedFix: Measure locally from the fetch: clamp with the contract's TTL (`Math.min(DOWNLOAD_URL_SECONDS * 1000, serverRemaining)`, exporting DOWNLOAD_URL_SECONDS through @pencillift/contracts), or start the timer from the response instant and keep `expiresAt` only for the displayed wall-clock time.

findings.title: After archiving, Homework and the learning planner label the child "no paid slot yet" and tell the parent to assign a slot they cannot assign
