findings.title: A child-scope deletion leaves the child's paid slot assigned; activate on a sibling then tells the parent to buy capacity they already pay for, and no route can free it
findings.mechanism: public.request_deletion (migration 0840, the current definition) archives the child and revokes its sessions/devices/jobs/assignments but never touches public.child_slot_assignments — only the purge (app.purge_family_data, 0620/0710/0820) deletes those rows. Meanwhile family.ts:359-368 decides capacity from `count(*) from child_slot_assignments where released_at is null` against family_capacity.paid_slots. So while the deletion is `requested`/`processing` the freed child still occupies a paid slot. Both routes that could release it are now closed: POST /children/:id/activate goes through the new visibleChild() and answers 404 for that child (family.ts:349), and POST /children/:id/archive only releases the slot inside `if (child.status !== 'archived')` (family.ts:392) — request_deletion already set the status to 'archived', so the whole release block, including `update child_slot_assignments set released_at = now(), release_reason = 'archived'`, is skipped and the route returns a slotSummary that still counts the slot. The parent has no way out; the slot frees only when the deletion_purge job succeeds, and if that job exhausts its retries (max_attempts, status failed_final/dead_letter) the paid slot is consumed permanently with no parent-visible remedy.
findings.repro: Family with paid_slots = 1, child A active holding the one slot, sibling B draft. Parent requests deletion of A (POST /v1/deletion {scope:'child',childId:A} -> 202). Parent then activates B: POST /v1/children/B/activate. The capacity query returns paid_slots=1, open=1, so the route throws businessRule('NEEDS_PAID_SLOT', 'All 1 paid child slots are in use. Add a child slot to your plan first.') — a 422 telling the parent to buy a second $9.99 slot. POST /v1/children/A/archive answers 200 and changes nothing (status is already 'archived'), and POST /v1/children/A/activate answers 404.
findings.proof:
psql on pl_scratch_r2 (migrated schema), inside a rolled-back transaction, replaying exactly what request_deletion does for scope='child' (insert deletion_requests + `update child_profiles set status='archived'`) and then running the activate route's own capacity query:

 paid_slots | open_assignments 
------------+------------------
          1 |                1

 status  
----------
 archived

               child_id               | released_at | release_reason 
--------------------------------------+-------------+----------------
 77777777-7777-4777-8777-777777777777 |             | 

open_assignments = 1 >= paid_slots = 1 is exactly the NEEDS_PAID_SLOT branch (family.ts:362). released_at is still null after the archive route's guard would have skipped its block. `grep -rn child_slot_assignments supabase/migrations/*.sql` shows the only writers are 0200 (table/trigger), the archive route, activate, and the three purge definitions — request_deletion is absent from every version (0600, 0620, 0710, 0820, 0840).
findings.suggestedFix: Release the slot at request time, where the rest of the "stop processing immediately" work already happens: add `update public.child_slot_assignments set released_at = now(), release_reason = 'deletion' where family_id = p_family and released_at is null and (p_child is null or child_id = p_child);` to public.request_deletion in a new migration (and give release_reason's check constraint that value). Independently, make the archive route's release idempotent — move the `update child_slot_assignments ... where released_at is null` out of the `if (child.status !== 'archived')` block in apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:392 so an already-archived child with a stuck open assignment can still be reconciled.
findings.leadDecision: Release the child paid slot in the SAME transaction as the child-scope deletion request, so capacity a family pays for is not stranded and no sibling is told to buy more.

findings.title: Lock-order inversion between the new PATCH /v1/children/:childId (families FOR UPDATE, then the child row) and POST /children/:childId/pairing-code (child row, then families via the FK) deadlocks
findings.mechanism: PATCH /v1/children/:childId takes `select 1 from public.families ... for update` (family.ts:238) and only afterwards `update public.child_profiles` (which takes FOR NO KEY UPDATE on the child row). POST /children/:childId/pairing-code does the opposite, deliberately: it takes the child row first (`for no key update`, family.ts:319, the BUG-106 fix) and then inserts into private.child_pairing_codes, whose `family_id uuid not null references public.families (id)` (migration 0001:312) makes Postgres take FOR KEY SHARE on the same families row — which FOR UPDATE blocks. The two orders are a textbook ABBA cycle, so one transaction is killed with SQLSTATE 40P01. L-021 (BUG-106) recorded that other parent-locking paths were swept and "no other inversion found", but that sweep looked at triggers, not at the FK lock the pairing-code INSERT itself takes on families. POST /children/:id/activate (family.ts:344) and POST /children/:id/archive (family.ts:388) have the same families-first order, so they are in the cycle too. app.ts:176 maps 40P01 to PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, so the victim's request answers 503 'The service is busy. Please try again.' with Retry-After: 1 — and in the repro the victim was the families-first side, i.e. the parent's profile edit / slot activation / archive, not the pairing request.
findings.repro: Two connections against the migrated schema, one family F and one child C: (A) BEGIN; select 1 from families where id=F for update; [pause]; update child_profiles set nickname='Edited' where id=C. (B) [starts during A's pause] BEGIN; select 1 from child_profiles where id=C for no key update; insert into private.child_pairing_codes (family_id, child_id, code_hash, created_by, expires_at) values (F, C, ...). B blocks on the FK's FOR KEY SHARE on F; A then blocks on C; the deadlock detector kills A.
findings.proof:
Ran the two scripts concurrently on pl_scratch_r2 (files kept at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-claudecampsophie/b1b9c04d-3d1c-58be-b925-a948687d722a/scratchpad/hardening/hunt-r4/api-family-learning/{a,b}.sql,{a,b}.out). Session A printed:

ERROR:  deadlock detected
DETAIL:  Process 20906 waits for ShareLock on transaction 3042551; blocked by process 20905.
Process 20905 waits for ShareLock on transaction 3042550; blocked by process 20906.
CONTEXT:  while locking tuple (0,1) in relation "child_profiles"

Session B printed `INSERT 0 1` / `B committed`. So the families-first transaction (PATCH/activate/archive) is the victim and answers 503.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the pairing-code transaction the same first lock as the other family writes: in apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:318-320, take `select 1 from public.families where id = ${familyId} for no key update` BEFORE the `select 1 from public.child_profiles ... for no key update`. That keeps BUG-106's invariant (child row still locked before any code row) and removes the cycle. Alternatively drop the families FOR UPDATE from PATCH /children/:childId, which only needs to serialise against activate/archive on the child row itself — but then activate and archive still need the family lock, so locking families first everywhere is the cheaper rule.
findings.leadDecision: One lock order everywhere for these rows. Pick the order the older routes already use and change the new PATCH to match; say in a comment which order is canonical.

findings.title: The two new PATCH write routes have no rate limit, unlike every sibling parent write, and each one appends an audit_events row that nothing prunes
findings.mechanism: Every other parent write in these two files reserves a per-family bound before doing work: POST /children uses RATE_RULES.childCreatePerFamily (family.ts:190), POST /children/:id/pairing-code uses pairingCreatePerFamily (family.ts:282), and learning.ts gates subject/test-date/study-material creates and even the update-only PUT /learning-schedule through familyWriteLimit (scheduleUpdatePerFamily). The new PATCH /v1/family (family.ts:158) and PATCH /v1/children/:childId (family.ts:228) call neither enforceRateLimit nor familyWriteLimit, and app.ts installs no global per-user limiter. Each call writes one public.audit_events row (family.ts:176 and 254). audit_events has no Data-API hourly bound in migration 0860 (which covers child_subjects, test_dates, study_materials, learning_schedules, rewards, support_cases, support_case_messages) and no retention sweep in 0680_retention.sql, so the rows are permanent. RATE_RULES' own comment states the project rule being broken: 'Parent create routes, per family (API-AUTH-R1-04; spec: every endpoint defines a limit)'.
findings.repro: A signed-in parent with a recent adult unlock loops `PATCH /v1/family {"displayName":"a"}` (or `PATCH /v1/children/<id> {"nickname":"a"}`). Every request answers 200 and inserts one audit_events row; nothing refuses the 1000th or the 100000th, and each also takes a FOR UPDATE on the family row, serialising the family's other writes behind it.
findings.proof: Code read: `grep -n "enforceRateLimit\|familyWriteLimit" apps/api/src/routes/family.ts` shows hits only in POST /children (190) and POST /children/:id/pairing-code (282) — neither PATCH handler. `grep -n "rateLimit\|enforceRateLimit\|RATE_RULES" apps/api/src/app.ts` prints nothing, so there is no global limiter. `grep -rn audit_events supabase/migrations/0680_retention.sql supabase/migrations/0860_hardening_r2_db.sql` finds only an audit INSERT in 0680 and a comment in 0860 — no bound and no prune for that table.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a per-family rule (e.g. RATE_RULES.profileUpdatePerFamily = { limit: 30, windowSeconds: 3600 }) and call enforceRateLimit/familyWriteLimit at the top of both PATCH handlers, after currentFamilyId and before readJson, the same shape POST /children uses.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: PATCH /v1/children/:childId answers 404 'Child not found' for a child that the same API lists with deletionPending: true, so the parent is told the profile is gone
findings.mechanism: visibleChild() (family.ts:40-58) hides a child under an open deletion and its doc states the reason: 'Returns undefined for an unknown id, another family's child and a child under deletion alike, so a caller learns nothing from the difference (NOT_FOUND on every one).' That reasoning is sound for activate and pairing-code as an anti-enumeration measure, but it does not hold for the profile edit of the caller's OWN child: the same round deliberately keeps that child in GET /v1/family and marks it `deletionPending: true` (family.ts:113-125, packages/contracts/src/family.ts:79), so the response has already disclosed to this exact caller that the child exists and is under deletion. Nothing is protected by the 404, and the cost is a wrong message: the immediately adjacent archived case gets a truthful 422 businessRule('CHILD_ARCHIVED', ...) (family.ts:242-247) while the deletion-pending case claims the profile does not exist.
findings.repro: Family with children Riley and Sam. POST /v1/deletion {scope:'child', childId: Riley} -> 202. GET /v1/family -> children includes {id: Riley, nickname:'Riley', status:'archived', deletionPending:true}. PATCH /v1/children/<Riley> {gradeLevel: 7} -> 404 {error:{code:'NOT_FOUND', message:'Child not found'}}. A parent on a tab opened before the request (the web hides the control only after a refetch; apps/web/src/pages/app/ChildrenPage.tsx:305) taps Save and is told the child they can still see in the list does not exist.
findings.proof: Pinned by the round's own test, apps/api/tests/family-profile.review.test.ts:254 ('refuses a profile edit while the deletion is open' expects 404) together with :295 ('keeps the child in GET /v1/family, flagged, so the privacy screens can still name it', expecting nickname 'Riley', status 'archived', deletionPending true). Both assertions pass at 8bc022b: `pnpm --filter @pencillift/api exec vitest run tests/family-profile.review.test.ts --reporter=default` -> 19 passed. So one response names the child while the other denies it exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep visibleChild() as the gate for activate and pairing-code, but in PATCH /v1/children/:childId separate the two cases: look the child up by (id, family_id) with the families deleted_at join, and when a deletion covering it is open throw a BUSINESS_RULE with a stable rule code (e.g. 'CHILD_DELETION_PENDING', message 'This child's data is being deleted, so the profile can no longer be changed'), the same shape as CHILD_ARCHIVED. An id that is unknown or another family's still answers NOT_FOUND, so nothing new is enumerable.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

areas.title: Child-safety screening, consent withdrawal and the parent report list (apps/api/src/routes/privacy.ts, guardians.ts; packages/ai/src/moderation.ts; safety half of apps/api/src/jobs/scan-process.ts)

findings.title: The new oldest-end unresolved bound does not drain for parent-filed reports, so a newer safety flag is permanently hidden from the family list
findings.mechanism: GET /v1/safety-reports (privacy.ts:761-780) now returns `unresolved` = the 200 OLDEST rows with status <> 'resolved', plus the 100 newest resolved. The comment at 122-132 justifies the oldest-end bound with "the bound drains — every report a grown-up acts on makes room for the next". That is false for reporter_kind = 'parent': the guardian action path refuses them outright (privacy.ts:815-820, PRIVACY_RULES.parentActionNotForReport), and migration 0790's safety_reports_resolution_shape only permits a resolution on 'system' and 'child' reports ("a parent's own report is closed by the reviewer"). So a parent-filed report can never leave the unresolved set through any family-facing surface — only the owner-admin queue can resolve it. Once 200 unresolved parent reports exist, every LATER system flag and every later child report falls outside the window and is absent from the response. The web portal (apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:236) and the mobile app (apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.ts:281) build the actionable list solely from this response and PATCH per listed report, and the guardian flag email links to /app/privacy (apps/api/src/jobs/dispatcher.ts:388), so a flag outside the window is unreachable and unactionable from every product surface. This is the exact failure CS-R2-07 set out to remove (a cap hiding work a grown-up must act on), reintroduced from the other end. Reaching 200 is cheap: POST /v1/safety-reports is rate-limited at 30/hour PER USER (privacy.ts:62), so one guardian fills the window in under 7 hours and two in ~3.5 — the abuse case matters because an adult who is the subject of a child's disclosure can pre-fill the window so that future flags on that child never appear in the family list.
findings.repro: 1. Guardian A posts 200 reports to POST /v1/safety-reports (30/hour). All land status='open', reporter_kind='parent'. 2. The scan job then files a system flag on a child's answer (status='escalated', family_visible=true) and enqueues safety_flag_email. 3. GET /v1/safety-reports as either guardian: the 200 older open parent rows fill the unresolved CTE; the flag is not in `reports`. 4. The guardian receives the email, opens /app/privacy, sees no flag. PATCH /v1/safety-reports/:id on any of the 200 parent rows returns 422 parentActionNotForReport, so nothing they can do frees a slot.
findings.proof: psql 16 (local) simulation of the exact CTE shape, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-claudecampsophie/b1b9c04d-3d1c-58be-b925-a948687d722a/scratchpad/hardening/hunt-r4/cs/list.sql: 200 'parent'/'open' rows dated before one 'system'/'escalated' row and one 'child'/'open' row, then `with unresolved as (... order by created_at asc limit 200), newest_resolved as (...) select count(*), bool_or(id=9001), bool_or(id=9002) from (union all)`. Printed: `returned=200 | system_flag_listed=f | child_report_listed=f`. Code proof of the non-draining half: privacy.ts:815-820 throws businessRule(parentActionNotForReport) for reporter_kind='parent', and supabase/migrations/0790_parent_flag_review.sql:33-42 forbids any resolution on a parent report. The round's own test acknowledges the gap by resolving the filler rows with raw SQL instead of the action path — apps/api/tests/privacy-r2.review.test.ts:624-626 "(the query is what is under test here, not the action path)" — and its only flag-visibility case puts the flag OLDER than the filler rows, so the newer-flag case is untested.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not let rows the family cannot act on consume the bound. Either (a) partition the list: always return every report the family can act on (reporter_kind in ('system','child') and status <> 'resolved') with no cap or with keyset paging (BUG-117), and cap the guardian's own pending reports separately; or (b) order the unresolved CTE by actionability first — `order by (reporter_kind = 'parent'), created_at asc` — so parent rows are the ones squeezed out, never a system flag. Either way add an API test whose flag is NEWER than UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE unresolved parent reports.
findings.leadDecision: Bound per reporter kind, not as one page: unresolved SYSTEM flags oldest-first (the family can address or clear those, so the bound drains), plus the NEWEST unresolved parent- and child-filed reports (the family cannot resolve their own report — only staff can — so newest is what they need), plus the newest resolved as today. The regression test must NOT resolve rows with raw SQL to prove the drain: prove that a NEW system flag is listed while 200+ open parent reports exist. The lead wrote the defect and the too-kind test; say so in the test comment.

findings.title: The new family_data export ships the child's safety-notice body, which encodes which kind of concern was flagged
findings.mechanism: CS-R2-05 added `childFeedback: select id, question_id, child_id, kind, body, created_at from public.child_feedback where family_id = ...` to the 'family_data' export with no filter on `kind`, so every row with kind='safety' is exported verbatim. That body is childSafetyMessage(screen.categories, ageBand) (packages/domain/src/safety/templates.ts:137-151), and its composition is a pure function of the screen categories: a self_harm flag adds the 988 line, an abuse/sexual/secrecy/personal_contact flag adds the Childhelp 1-800-422-4453 line and suppresses the anger line, a violence-only flag adds the anger line. Twelve lines below, the same commit's `safetyFlags` block claims the opposite guarantee — "no category, no screen_categories, no screen_version and no provider codes, so the export cannot say which kind of concern was flagged (CS-R2-02)" (export-build.ts:529-532) — while still exporting `feedback_id`, which joins each flag to the exact notice row. So the round-3 fix that removed the screen codes from the family-readable audit row (apps/api/src/jobs/scan-process.ts:2219-2250, which correctly writes the reviewer-only row with family_id = null) is defeated by the sibling surface the same round opened. This breaks the project rule that the family never learns WHICH KIND of safety concern, and it matters most in the case the design exists for: the adult who reads the export may be the subject of the child's disclosure. It also now covers provider-only flags, since CS-R2-03 made an unmapped provider category fall back to violence+abuse (packages/ai/src/moderation.ts:128, 216-220), i.e. the Childhelp wording.
findings.repro: 1. A child's answer screens severe as self_harm on one question and as abuse on another; the scan job writes two child_feedback rows kind='safety' and two system reports. 2. Any guardian: POST /v1/exports {kind:'family_data'} after a PIN unlock, wait for export_build, download the JSON. 3. childFeedback[] contains both bodies; the one carrying "call or text 988" is the self-harm flag and the one carrying "Childhelp hotline at 1-800-422-4453" is the abuse-type flag, and safetyFlags[].feedback_id names which flag each belongs to.
findings.proof: node --experimental-strip-types on packages/domain/src/safety/templates.ts (scratchpad .../hunt-r4/cs/msg.mjs) printed the distinguishing sentence per category set for ageBand '8-10': self_harm -> "If you are thinking about hurting yourself, you can call or text 988 ..."; abuse+violence / sexual / secrecy / personal_contact -> "... call the Childhelp hotline at 1-800-422-4453 ..."; violence (alone) -> "If you are feeling very angry or upset, take a slow breath ...". Three distinguishable classes, one per notice. `git diff 110ff0f 8bc022b -- apps/api/src/jobs/export-build.ts` shows the childFeedback block is an addition in this round (+ at diff line 123), immediately followed by the CS-R2-02 no-category claim (+ at diff line 143).
findings.suggestedFix: Exclude the notice body from the export the way the screen columns are excluded: either `where kind <> 'safety'`, or export safety rows with the body replaced by the fixed generic sentence the parent list already shows (PARENT_SAFETY_FLAG_COPY.summary) and drop `feedback_id` from safetyFlags. Add an API test on the built family_data JSON asserting that no exported string contains '988' or '422-4453' when a flag exists, next to the existing CS-R2-02 audit-row test.
findings.leadDecision: The family-data export carries the FACT and instant of a safety notice and its template version, not the template body: the body wording encodes which kind of concern was flagged, which the family must never learn (owner decision 2026-09-25). The child key answers and feedback CS-R2-05 added stay.

findings.title: A scan stopped by consent withdrawal is explained to the parent as bad photos, and the advice it gives cannot work
findings.mechanism: settleScansAfterConsentWithdrawal (guardians.ts:84-123, new this round) ends every queued/extracting/checking initial scan as status='failed_final', error_code='CONSENT_REQUIRED'. The parent portal maps failed_final error codes in FAILED_FINAL_COPY (apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.tsx:126-134), which this round extended for the two codes the jobs fix introduced (SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS, AI_PAUSED_TOO_LONG) but has no line for CONSENT_REQUIRED, so explainStatus falls back to the state copy at HomeworkPage.tsx:110-112: "This scan could not be processed after several tries. Please start a new scan with clear photos." Neither clause is true — the scan was stopped once, by the family's own withdrawal, and the photos were fine — and the action it recommends cannot succeed: a new upload re-checks consent and is refused with the 422 business rule CONSENT_REQUIRED (packages/contracts/src/homework.ts:226). The copy also stays silent about the one good fact the settlement does deliver, that the page allowance was released (guardians.ts:116-119). The code was already reachable through the job's own assertActive path before this round, but the new settlement makes it the normal outcome for every pending scan at withdrawal rather than a rare race.
findings.repro: 1. A family with verified consent uploads a scan; the scan_process job is queued (assignment status 'queued'). 2. POST /v1/consent/withdraw with a recent PIN unlock. 3. The job is cancelled and the assignment becomes failed_final / CONSENT_REQUIRED. 4. Open the homework list in the portal: the scan reads "Could not finish — This scan could not be processed after several tries. Please start a new scan with clear photos." 5. Following that advice, a new scan upload is refused 422 CONSENT_REQUIRED.
findings.proof: Read-only inspection: guardians.ts:89 (`const CODE = 'CONSENT_REQUIRED'`) and 115 (`await move('failed_final')`); HomeworkPage.tsx:126-134 lists only FORMAT_NEEDS_CONVERSION, SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS and AI_PAUSED_TOO_LONG, and explainStatus (HomeworkPage.tsx:135-144) falls back to STATUS_COPY.failed_final (108-112). `grep -rn "CONSENT_REQUIRED" apps/web/src` returns no hit, so no other web surface supplies the wording.

findings.title: Churn dates a lapse by provider_updated_at, which is never the expiry instant: a subscription that simply ran out (or was transferred away) leaves both activeAtMonthStart and lapsedThisMonth
findings.mechanism: The BILL-R2-1-a CTE dates a terminal ledger row as `least(e.period_end, e.provider_updated_at)` and justifies it with "an expiry is observed at or after the nominal period end". That reasoning is false for this codebase. `provider_updated_at` is not an observation instant: mapRevenueCatSubscription (apps/api/src/providers/billing.ts:112-115) derives it as max(purchase_date, refunded_at, grace_period_expires_date, billing_issues_detected_at, unsubscribe_detected_at) and deliberately EXCLUDES expires_date. So for status 'expired' it is the cancellation instant (or, with no markers at all, the purchase instant) — always BEFORE period_end. For status 'revoked' vanishedSnapshots (billing-sync.ts:973) keeps the stored (old) provider instant on purpose, so a transfer-away is dated at the purchase too. orderCompleteFetch only overrides providerUpdatedAt when `snapshot.providerUpdatedAt < storedObservedAt` strictly, and here it is exactly equal, so nothing rewrites it. Consequence: `least(period_end, provider_updated_at)` = the cancellation/purchase date, which fails the base's `having bool_or(l.created_at < start and l.ended_at >= start)`. The family is therefore missing from activeAtMonthStart (the denominator) AND can never satisfy the `endedMs >= startMs` test at line 327-333, so it is missing from lapsedThisMonth too. Only 'refunded' rows are dated correctly (refunded_at is in the max), which is exactly the one case the new regression test covers. The three response definitions (lines 361, 366, 371) claim the opposite: "its period ran out, or it was revoked or refunded" and "whose paid access had not yet ended when the month began".
findings.repro: Family buys the $39.99 monthly product on 2026-08-05, turns auto-renew off on 2026-08-20, the period ends 2026-09-05; the sweep re-fetches and the row becomes status 'expired' with period_end 2026-09-05 and provider_updated_at 2026-08-20. Ask for /v1/admin/subscriptions (or /overview) at 2026-09-24. Expected activeAtMonthStart 1, lapsedThisMonth 1, churn 10000 (the family was paying on 1 September and left on 5 September). Actual activeAtMonthStart 0, lapsedThisMonth 0, churn null. Same for a family whose store subscription was transferred away in September (status 'revoked'). In the suite's own helper: entitlement(fam, { status: 'expired', createdAt: '2026-08-05T00:00:00Z', periodStart: '2026-08-05T00:00:00Z', periodEnd: '2026-09-05T00:00:00Z', providerUpdatedAt: '2026-08-20T00:00:00Z' }) with api.now.value = SEPTEMBER.
findings.proof: (1) Ran the REAL mapper (node --experimental-strip-types, importing apps/api/src/providers/billing.ts): scenario A (cancelled 20 Aug, expires 5 Sep) printed `status=expired periodEnd=2026-09-05T00:00:00.000Z providerUpdatedAt=2026-08-20T00:00:00.000Z => ended_at=2026-08-20T00:00:00.000Z`; scenario B (never cancelled, simply expired 6 Sep) printed `providerUpdatedAt=2026-08-06T00:00:00.000Z => ended_at=2026-08-06T00:00:00.000Z`. (2) Ran the baseFamilies query verbatim (with the families join) in local PG16 over two rows — A = the realistic expired row (provider_updated_at 2026-08-20) and R = the row the new test writes (provider_updated_at = the expiry 2026-09-05): the result set contained only R. A is absent from the base, so it is in neither figure. (3) The codebase's own test asserts this fallback: apps/api/tests/billing-hardening.review.test.ts:493 expects providerUpdatedAt to fall back to the purchase date 2026-09-10 when a marker is cleared. (4) apps/api/tests/billing-r2.review.test.ts passes (16/16) because every lapse fixture either keeps status 'active' or hand-sets providerUpdatedAt to the ending instant.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not date an ending from provider_updated_at. Either (a) date 'expired'/'revoked'/'refunded'/'billing_retry' as `greatest(e.period_end, least(e.period_end, e.provider_updated_at))` — i.e. period_end for an expiry, and provider_updated_at only when it is a mid-period ending (refunded_at/revocation strictly inside the period, detectable because refunded rows carry refunded_at in provider_updated_at) — or (b) add an explicit `ended_at` column written by reconcileEntitlements when a row leaves a granting status (the provider observation instant, i.e. fetched_at, bounded below by period_end for a plain expiry). Then add the missing regression: an 'expired' row whose provider_updated_at predates period_end must still be in activeAtMonthStart and must count as lapsed in the month period_end falls in.
findings.leadDecision: Date a lapse by when paid ACCESS ended, derived the same way the domain grant rule derives it, never by provider_updated_at alone. A subscription that simply ran out, or was transferred away, must be counted in the month access actually stopped.

findings.title: Refund and dispute amounts are still provider gross (sales tax included) while charged_amount_cents is now pre-tax, so a partial refund on a taxed invoice understates net revenue
findings.mechanism: BILL-R2-4 changed Stripe's chargedCents to the pre-tax subscription amount (subscriptionChargeCents, line 242) but the refund figures written next to it still come from the provider's tax-inclusive charge: webhooks.ts:340 passes `object.amount_refunded` (a Charge amount, tax included) and webhooks.ts:356 passes the Dispute `amount`. The new `least(charged_amount_cents, ...)` caps only stop the figure exceeding the charge; they do not convert units. For a FULL refund or a full dispute the cap makes the result exact (refunded = charged), so those are fine — but a PARTIAL refund records a tax-inclusive amount against a pre-tax gross, and loadRevenueMonths computes net = gross − refunds − fee from the same row, so net revenue is understated by the tax share of the refunded amount. Before the change the same asymmetry existed in the opposite direction (gross included retained tax), so this is a unit mismatch the fix left half-done, not a pre-existing one.
findings.repro: Stripe renewal: subscription line amount 3999, tax 330, charge amount 4329. Recorded charged_amount_cents = 3999. The owner refunds $20 of that charge: charge.refunded arrives with amount_refunded = 2000, amount = 4329 → not full → applyRefund('partial_refund', 2000) → refunded_cents = 2000 against a 3999 charge. /v1/admin/revenue then reports stripe net = 3999 − 2000 = 1999 for that period, although the pre-tax revenue PencilLift gave back is only ~1857 (the rest of the $20 was the state's tax) and the correct net is ~2142. The error is the tax fraction of every partial refund.
findings.proof: Read the whole path: webhooks.ts:338-348 (refunded = object.amount_refunded, full = refunded >= object.amount — both tax-inclusive Charge fields), billing-sync.ts:735-754 (the cap, applied to the pre-tax charged_amount_cents), ops-metrics.ts:176-200 (gross = sum(charged_amount_cents), refunds = sum(refunded_cents)) and packages/domain/src/ops/revenue.ts channelRevenue (net = gross − refunds − fee). No conversion exists anywhere between the two units; the comment at billing-sync.ts:716-722 states the mismatch but only guards the full-refund case with the cap.
findings.suggestedFix: Record the refund in the same unit as the charge: keep the invoice's tax figure on the billing_periods row (or store refunded_cents pre-tax by scaling the provider amount by charged/(charged+tax) with a documented rounding rule, capped at charged). Alternatively record refunded_cents gross together with a refunded_tax_cents column and subtract only the pre-tax part in loadRevenueMonths.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: chargedCents no longer reflects what Stripe collected: a renewal covered by a customer credit balance books full-price gross and earns the $1 school donation
findings.mechanism: subscriptionChargeCents now prefers the subscription line's own amount (net of that line's discounts) and never looks at what was actually paid, except as a last-resort fallback. A Stripe invoice can be settled partly from the customer's credit balance (invoice.starting_balance, produced when an earlier proration/credit exceeded that invoice's total): then total = 3999 while amount_due = amount_paid = 3999 − credit. The line amount is unaffected by the credit and carries no discount_amounts, so chargedCents = 3999. Downstream: billing_periods.charged_amount_cents (the owner's gross revenue, ops-metrics loadRevenueMonths) counts money not collected in that month, and evaluateDonationEligibility's regular_tier_price rule (chargedAmountCents === regularAmountCents, packages/domain/src/donations/eligibility.ts) now passes, so the $1 school accrual is created for a month whose cash collection was below the tier price. Under the previous `amount_paid` the same invoice failed the rule. (Stated assumption: Stripe applies a customer credit balance through starting_balance/amount_due, leaving line amounts and total_excluding_tax untouched.)
findings.repro: Family downgrades mid-cycle, leaving a $25 customer credit balance in Stripe. Next renewal invoice: subscription line amount 3999, tax 0, total 3999, starting_balance −2500, amount_due = amount_paid = 1499, no discounts. invoice.paid → mapStripeInvoiceToPeriod → chargedCents 3999 (branch 1, line.amount − no discounts) → recordBillingPeriod writes charged_amount_cents 3999, discount_cents 0 → the donation job sees charged 3999 == regular 3999, discountCents 0 → $1 accrues to the school and /v1/admin/revenue books 3999 gross for a month in which $14.99 was collected.
findings.proof: Code read of billing-sync.ts:236-256 (no reference to amount_paid unless BOTH line.amount and total_excluding_tax and subtotal are missing), 266-283 (chargedCents is the only amount written), 500-520 (recordBillingPeriod stores it as charged_amount_cents and computes discountCents from reportedDiscountCents, which a credit balance does not populate) and packages/domain/src/donations/eligibility.ts rules `undiscounted` / `regular_tier_price` (equality against regularAmountCents).
findings.suggestedFix: Take the pre-tax amount the invoice actually collected: min(subscription-line net, amount_paid − tax) when starting_balance is negative, or record the credit applied as a discountSource so the period is not treated as a full-price collected month. Whichever is chosen, state in the definition text whether gross means billed or collected, since loadRevenueMonths presents it as revenue.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: A refused webhook body now raises a billing_events_failed attention count the owner can never clear and cannot act on
findings.mechanism: BILL-R2-6 stores a schema-refused body as status 'failed' so the overview counts it. The row keeps only the digest (raw payloads are deliberately not stored, migration 0200 line 30), and there is no admin route over public.billing_provider_events at all (grep: the table is touched only by webhooks.ts and by the count in ops-metrics.ts:487). The only exit from 'failed' is recordEvent's re-open clause (line 122-129), which needs the provider to redeliver the SAME event id after a schema fix. Providers stop retrying after a bounded window (Stripe ~3 days), so once that window closes the row is stuck 'failed' for ever: attention item billing_events_failed shows a permanent non-zero count with an ever-growing oldestAgeHours, for work that cannot be done and an event whose content is unrecoverable. The attention list is the owner's work queue, so a permanently non-clearable entry hides genuinely new failures behind it (the rule is all-time and has no window, unlike jobs_failed which uses FAILED_JOBS_WINDOW_DAYS).
findings.repro: RevenueCat posts an event type whose body the schema refuses (e.g. a TRANSFER without transferred_to). traceRejectedEvent writes (revenuecat, <id>, failed, UNEXPECTED_SHAPE) and the route answers 400. RevenueCat retries for its window and gives up. GET /v1/admin/overview then lists attention kind billing_events_failed count 1 for ever; there is no endpoint to list, replay or dismiss it, and no payload to replay. After ten such events over a year the count reads 10 and the owner cannot tell whether any of them is current.
findings.proof: grep for `billing_provider_events` across apps, packages, supabase and scripts returns only webhooks.ts (insert/update), ops-metrics.ts (count + definition) and migration 0200 (table, RLS, admin read policy) — no list/retry/dismiss route. ops-metrics.ts:485-489 counts `where status = 'failed'` with no time window, and attention.ts has no window constant for this kind (FAILED_JOBS_WINDOW_DAYS applies only to jobs_failed).
findings.suggestedFix: Give the rule an exit: either window it (count only rows received within N days, as jobs_failed does), or add an owner-visible list with an explicit acknowledge/dismiss that sets a terminal status (e.g. 'ignored' with error_code kept plus acknowledged_at), so the attention item can return to zero once the owner has read it. Keep the count honest by reporting acknowledged shapes separately.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: The owner overview now materializes one row per family per query where it previously counted in SQL
findings.mechanism: BILL-R2-1 replaced three scalar sub-selects (new_this_month, lapsed_this_month, active_at_start were `count(*)::int`) with two queries that return a row per family — newFamilies (line 273) has no LIMIT and no predicate that bounds its size, and baseFamilies (line 293) returns every family that had a non-pending row created before the month, with the counting then done in JS (lines 327-335). Together with the pre-existing `active` query (a row per granting entitlement) the overview handler holds three arrays proportional to the whole customer base inside one Worker invocation, whose memory is capped (128 MB) and which also holds six months of revenue rows and the whole month's revenue_entries (loadRecognizedRevenue). Growth is linear in families, so the route degrades quietly as the business grows rather than at a threshold that a test would catch.
findings.repro: At 200k families with one ledger row each, GET /v1/admin/overview issues `select e.family_id from public.family_entitlements group by e.family_id having …` and the baseFamilies CTE, each returning up to 200k rows that are decoded into JS objects, to produce two integers. The previous implementation returned one row of three integers for the same figures.
findings.proof: Diff read of 110ff0f..8bc022b for ops-metrics.ts: the removed block is `select (select count(*)::int …) as new_this_month, (…) as lapsed_this_month, (…) as active_at_start`; the added queries select family_id (and ended_at) per family and the arithmetic moved to `baseFamilies.filter(...).length` / `newFamilies.length`. No LIMIT appears in either new query.
findings.suggestedFix: Push the counting back into SQL: keep the same ledger CTE but aggregate it (`select count(*) filter (where ended_at >= :start and ended_at <= :now and not granting_now) as lapsed, count(*) as base from base_families`), computing the "grants access now" predicate in the CTE instead of a JS set, so the route returns scalars again.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: The truncation retry at a raised output budget is unreachable for extraction and grading: the stage cost cap always refuses it, so the first cut-off answer ends the scan
findings.mechanism: runStage raises the output budget to `limits.maxOutputTokens * OUTPUT_TRUNCATED_BUDGET_MULTIPLE` (= 2x) after a `max_output_tokens` incomplete, and the next loop turn asks canAttempt whether `spentSoFar + nextEstimate <= limits.maxCostMicros` (packages/domain/src/quotas/stages.ts:104). For extraction and grading the stage caps are 150,000 micros with maxOutputTokens 4,000 on gpt-5.6-terra ($12/M out, $2/M in), so 3 x output alone is 144,000 micros and only 6,000 micros (3,000 input tokens) of headroom is left for TWO attempts' input. The real caller always passes `inputTokenUpperBound(prompt, input)` (scan-process.ts:1190), whose FLOOR — instructions + strict schema + one two-byte text part, zero images, zero questions — is already 2,478 tokens for extraction and 2,301 for grading. So the raise is refused every time, at every real input size; the stage returns OUTPUT_TRUNCATED after ONE call and scan-process.ts:1213 turns it into PermanentFailure('SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS') -> failed_final. A worksheet whose extraction is a few hundred tokens over 4,000 is abandoned (web copy: 'split it into two scans with fewer pages each') although a single retry at 8,000 tokens would very likely have transcribed it. Only verification (cap 100,000, output 2,000) can ever take the raise. The doc comment at run.ts:49-64 and the scan comment at 1209-1212 both assert the raised attempt already happened.
findings.repro: Scratch vitest in apps/api/src/jobs (deleted again; `git status --porcelain` clean afterwards) computing, per stage, inputTokenUpperBound(PROMPTS[stage], [{type:'input_text',text:'{}'}]) then estimateUpperBoundCostMicros for maxOutputTokens and 2x, then canAttempt({attemptsSoFar:1, spentMicrosSoFar:est1, nextEstimateMicros:est2}).
findings.suggestedFix: Either size the multiple to the headroom that exists (e.g. raise only to `min(2 * maxOutputTokens, floor((maxCostMicros - spent - inputMicros) / outputRate))`, so a partial raise is still attempted), or lift extraction/grading maxCostMicros to admit 2x output (>= ~160,000), or drop the raise for those stages and say so in the comment. In any case make the truncation test use `inputTokenUpperBound(PROMPTS.extraction, input)` as the caller does, so a cap that cannot admit the raise fails the test.
findings.leadDecision: The one raised retry must be ADMISSIBLE: allow the raised estimate within the stage cost cap for that single retry, or drop the retry and settle at once with the parent-facing code. An unreachable branch is not an option.

findings.title: A repeated printed question number is always treated as a second section, never as the model transcribing the same question twice, so a duplicate row is stored, shown to the child and drags the whole scan into parent review
findings.mechanism: storeQuestions used to drop a second question with the same (pageNumber, questionNumber) ('keep the first'). It now calls disambiguate(), stores the later one under `<number>#2` and forces `uncertainty = 'high'` (line 1407). Nothing compares promptText or studentAnswerText, so the two very different causes of a repeated label are treated identically: a genuine Part A/Part B restart, and the extraction model listing one question twice (the case the removed dedup existed for). For the repetition: the phantom row is inserted, it is included in the grading AND verification requests (it has a non-blank answer and a grading result, so it lands in `pending`, grade() line ~1543), its uncertainty 'high' becomes capture ['answer_source_uncertain'], gradeObjectiveQuestion returns unresolved/ANSWER_SOURCE_UNCERTAIN (packages/domain/src/grading/grade.ts:118-123 — capture wins over any grade, so even a bare-arithmetic prompt key cannot decide it), resolveGrading returns {final:'unresolved', route:'parent_review'} (resolve.ts:114-116), and finish() line 1755 therefore transitions the assignment to needs_parent_review instead of ready. The child also sees a duplicate question card, an extra public.attempts row with correctness 'unresolved' is written as skill evidence (recordAttempt), and the duplicate consumes grading and verification output tokens — which makes the very truncation of finding R4-JOBS-1 more likely.
findings.repro: Extraction returns two identical entries for page 1: [{pageNumber:1, questionNumber:'3', promptText:'7 x 8 =', studentAnswerText:'54', answerKind:'numeric', uncertainty:'low'}, {the same object again}]. Stored: question_number '3' (uncertainty low) and '3#2' (uncertainty forced high). The '3#2' row resolves to unresolved/parent_review, so a scan whose real questions were all graded ends in needs_parent_review with a phantom question.
findings.proof: Code path read end to end: scan-process.ts:1394-1410 (no promptText comparison anywhere in disambiguate(), lines 1434-1458) -> grade() capture branch (missingPassage/uncertainty==='high' -> ['answer_source_uncertain']) -> packages/domain/src/grading/grade.ts:118-123 `captureOutcome` returns outcome('unresolved','ANSWER_SOURCE_UNCERTAIN') BEFORE any answer check, so `decisive(outcome.verdict)` is false and `deterministic` stays undefined -> packages/domain/src/grading/resolve.ts:114-116 returns resolution('unresolved','parent_review') -> scan-process.ts:1753-1756 `needsReview` true -> transition('needs_parent_review'). The pre-change line was `if (!pageId || seen.has(key)) continue; // unknown page or duplicate label: keep the first` (git show 110ff0f:apps/api/src/jobs/scan-process.ts).
findings.suggestedFix: Only disambiguate when the repeat is a different question: keep the first when the new entry's promptText (and studentAnswerText) match an already-stored entry with that page and number — trimmed/casefolded — and store `<number>#2` only when they differ. That keeps DB-R2-06's Part A/Part B fix and restores the dedup for a model that repeats itself.
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: The spend-pause counter counts every processing cycle, not pauses, so a scan that already failed retryably starts its ceiling backoff at 6 hours and is abandoned after ~4 pauses instead of 8
findings.mechanism: countPause() for an initial run returns `this.ctx.processingAttempts + 1`, i.e. the durable `assignments.processing_attempts` column. That column is incremented by EVERY transition to 'extracting' (line 856 `processing_attempts = processing_attempts + ${to === 'extracting' ? 1 : 0}`), which includes every ordinary retryable failure (enterExtracting takes failed_retryable -> queued -> extracting) and every crashed-worker restart, not just spend-ceiling pauses. The pause wait is `min(6h, 1h * 2 ** (pauses - 1))` (line 953) and the scan is settled with AI_PAUSED_TOO_LONG once `pauses > 8` (line 938). The comment at 930-935 states processing_attempts is 'the durable count' of pauses, which it is not.
findings.repro: A scan whose grading stage fails retryably four times (GRADING_PROVIDER_FAILED; jobs.max_attempts default 5, migration 0600:97) has processing_attempts = 5 when the owner's ceiling is next reached. countPause() returns 5: the FIRST pause waits min(6h, 1h*2^4 = 16h) = 6h instead of 1h, and only pauses 5,6,7,8 remain, so the scan is failed_final with AI_PAUSED_TOO_LONG after ~24h instead of the intended ~37h over 8 pauses — its allowance is released and the parent is told to send the pages again, while a clean scan of the same family survives the same ceiling.
findings.proof: Read of scan-process.ts:852-861 (the increment is on any transition to 'extracting'), 884-890 (enterExtracting re-enters extracting on every retry), 937-959 and 967-977; migration 0100_learning.sql:91 (`processing_attempts smallint not null default 0`); grep shows no other writer and no reset of the column. Arithmetic: 1h*2^(5-1) = 16h -> clamped to SPEND_CEILING_MAX_RETRY_MS = 6h; 8 - 5 + 1 = 4 remaining pauses.
findings.suggestedFix: Count pauses in their own durable counter (a `spend_pauses` column, or the jobs row's last_error_code history) rather than reusing processing_attempts — or, minimally, have the initial-run pause path increment and read the same dedicated counter that countPause() already writes for a recheck (line 971-976).
findings.leadDecision: No lead constraint: take the cheapest change that closes the mechanism, with a failing test first. Do not widen the surface.

findings.title: The entitlement sweep was moved behind a job ledger that is allowed to consume the whole 15-minute invocation, so it gets zero time on any tick that claims a scan late
findings.mechanism: The same change moved `reconcileStaleEntitlements` after `runJobs` (line 1303) and let runJobs claim work until `elapsed > TICK_CLAIM_BUDGET_MS` (10 min) as long as the kind's worst case fits `TICK_WALL_LIMIT_MS - elapsed` (line 726). scan_process declares a 7-minute worst case, so a scan may still be claimed at elapsed = 8 min and run to exactly the 15-minute wall limit. The entitlements step then starts at or past the wall and the Cron invocation is killed before it issues a single provider request, so `entitlementsReconciled` is 0 and no family's ledger is refreshed on that tick. Consequence when the queue is deep in scans: a family whose store subscription lapsed without a webhook keeps its `active` children (and therefore paid AI, which assertActive(paidAi) would otherwise refuse) until a tick with a lighter queue happens to run the sweep.
findings.repro: Tick where earlier steps take ~1 min and the ledger has queued scans: claims run until elapsed 8 min, the last claim is a scan_process job (JOB_WORST_CASE_MS 7 min <= remaining 7 min), the scan runs its extraction + grading + verification + coaching calls to ~15 min, runJobs returns, and `step('entitlements', ...)` is entered with no wall time left.
findings.proof: Read of dispatcher.ts:74-91 (TICK_CLAIM_BUDGET_MS 10 min, TICK_WALL_LIMIT_MS 15 min, scan_process 7 min), 719-731 (the claim filter admits scan_process while elapsed <= 8 min), 1294-1305 (jobs step then entitlements step), and 1000-1035 (the sweep makes up to 25 sequential provider calls). 8 min + 7 min = 15 min = the declared invocation limit, so the budget arithmetic itself leaves the last step nothing.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve wall time for the steps that follow the ledger: pass runJobs a claim deadline of TICK_WALL_LIMIT_MS minus the worst case of the trailing steps (or keep the claim budget but subtract a trailing reserve from `remaining`), or move entitlements back before the ledger and bound it by its own deadline instead.
findings.leadDecision: The provider sweep must not be starvable: give it a reserved slice of the tick, or run it before the ledger with a hard total bound. Say which and why in a comment.

findings.title: DB-R2-04's revoke sweep stopped at tables: anon/authenticated still hold UPDATE on the append-only ledgers' identity sequences, so one statement as `authenticated` permanently breaks audit_events, ai_usage_events and points_ledger appends
findings.mechanism: Section 2 revokes TRUNCATE/TRIGGER/REFERENCES on all public TABLES (line 92) and in the table default privileges (lines 99-100), on the stated threat model "one SQL-injection bug on a path that runs as `authenticated`" (the API opens parent transactions with `set local role authenticated`, apps/api/src/db.ts:54). It does not touch SEQUENCE privileges. The shim / hosted Supabase default privileges grant ALL on sequences (supabase/tests/shim/supabase_platform_shim.sql:108), so anon and authenticated hold USAGE, SELECT and UPDATE on public.audit_events_id_seq, public.ai_usage_events_id_seq and public.points_ledger_id_seq — the identity sequences of exactly the three append-only ledgers 0860's own header names as the evidence it is protecting. UPDATE on a sequence is all setval() needs; it needs no privilege on the table, so app.prevent_mutation() and the revoked INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants are irrelevant. Resetting the sequence to 1 makes every later append fail on audit_events_pkey until an operator repairs it. The project already knows this rule: migration 0640_monetization.sql:671 does `revoke all on sequence public.aggregate_ad_events_id_seq from anon, authenticated, pl_child;` — the newer ledgers' sequences were simply never given the same treatment, and 0860 added a schema_invariants case for tables without a sibling case for sequences. The sequence default ACL is still `anon=rwU/postgres` and `authenticated=rwU/postgres`, so any future public table with a bigint identity/serial column is exposed again with no migration line and no failing test.
findings.repro: Probe DB pl_probe860 = shim + all migrations at 8bc022b, seeded with one family/child. (1) `begin; set_config('request.jwt.claims', '{"role":"authenticated","sub":...}'); set local role authenticated; select setval('public.audit_events_id_seq', 1, false); commit;` -> succeeds, returns 1. (2) Then, as the caller's own parent role, `select public.request_deletion('<family>')` (spec P4 "delete my data") -> ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "audit_events_pkey", DETAIL: Key (id)=(1) already exists, CONTEXT: ... insert into public.audit_events ... PL/pgSQL function public.request_deletion(uuid,uuid) line 54. The same failure hits every transaction that appends an audit row (create_family, device.paired, activation, consent) and, on ai_usage_events_id_seq, hits settleSpend's cost insert — which then keeps the spend hold to the end of the month (apps/api/src/jobs/spend-ceiling.ts:265), so the owner's AI budget is silently consumed by holds that will never settle.
findings.proof: Ran in psql against pl_probe860. ACL dump: `select c.relname, pg_get_userbyid(a.grantee), a.privilege_type from pg_class c, aclexplode(c.relacl) a where c.relkind='S' and c.relnamespace='public'::regnamespace` printed USAGE/SELECT/UPDATE for both `anon` and `authenticated` on ai_usage_events_id_seq, audit_events_id_seq and points_ledger_id_seq, and only postgres/service_role on aggregate_ad_events_id_seq (the one 0640 revoked). Default ACLs: `select d.defaclobjtype, unnest(d.defaclacl)::text from pg_default_acl d join pg_namespace n on n.oid=d.defaclnamespace where n.nspname='public'` printed `S | anon=rwU/postgres`, `S | authenticated=rwU/postgres` (w = UPDATE) alongside the cleaned `r | authenticated=arwd/postgres`. setval as `authenticated` returned 1; the subsequent request_deletion aborted with audit_events_pkey as quoted above. Also checked and confirmed NOT exploitable by the same route: `set local session_replication_role = replica` as authenticated -> "permission denied to set parameter", and `delete from public.audit_events` as authenticated -> "permission denied for table audit_events".
findings.suggestedFix: In a follow-up migration: `revoke all on all sequences in schema public from anon, authenticated, pl_child;` and `alter default privileges in schema public revoke all on sequences from anon, authenticated;` (service_role keeps them, as it does for tables). Extend supabase/tests/schema_invariants.test.ts with the sibling of the two DB-R2-04 cases: no client role in pg_class ACLs for relkind='S' in public, and no client-role entry in pg_default_acl where defaclobjtype='S'.
findings.leadDecision: Migration 0870 (the lead assigns this number) revokes UPDATE and USAGE on every sequence in public from anon, authenticated and pl_child, and a new schema_invariants case fails CI if a client role regains either.

findings.title: The one client DELETE grant in the guarded set is left unguarded: the Data API can delete an archived child's test dates, which the API refuses with CHILD_ARCHIVED
findings.mechanism: 0860 section 3b moves the archived-child / child-under-deletion rule into BEFORE triggers, but `test_dates_data_api_guard` is created `before insert` only (line 291). public.test_dates is the single table in the guarded set where `authenticated` holds DELETE (supabase/migrations/0100_learning.sql:499, a table-level grant), and the RLS policy test_dates_member is `for all` with `using (app.is_family_member(family_id))`, so the delete passes. The API's own path refuses it: apps/api/src/routes/learning.ts:827 `DELETE /children/:childId/test-dates/:testDateId` calls `ownedChild(c, 'write')`, which throws CHILD_ARCHIVED for an archived profile (learning.ts:211) and NOT_FOUND for a child under a child-scope deletion request (learning.ts:206-209). So the invariant 0860 set out to enforce — "an archived profile is history only: its parents read it, nothing changes it" (learning.ts:155) — is still skippable by a direct PostgREST request with the parent's own JWT, which is the exact class DB-R2-05 exists to close. Because public.request_deletion archives the target child (0620_deletion_purge.sql:112), the same DELETE also works while a child-scope deletion is requested/processing, i.e. while spec P4 says processing has stopped.
findings.repro: As authenticated in the caller's own family, with the child set to status='archived': `insert into public.test_dates (family_id, child_id, subject_id, test_date) values (...)` is refused ('the child profile is archived: nothing new can be added or changed for it'), but `delete from public.test_dates where id = '<archived child's test date>'` succeeds (DELETE 1) and the row is gone. The parent-facing API call for the same action returns CHILD_ARCHIVED.
findings.proof: Ran in psql against pl_probe860: seeded child_subjects + test_dates for child 3333...3333, then `update public.child_profiles set status='archived'`. Inside a transaction with role authenticated and the parent's jwt claims, the INSERT printed `ERROR: the child profile is archived: nothing new can be added or changed for it / CONTEXT: PL/pgSQL function app.assert_parent_child_write(uuid,uuid) line 14 at RAISE`, while the following `delete from public.test_dates where id='5555...5555'` printed `DELETE 1` and `select count(*) from public.test_dates` printed 0. Grant confirmed with information_schema.role_table_grants: test_dates | authenticated | DELETE,SELECT.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the trigger `before insert or delete on public.test_dates` and, in the DELETE branch, call `app.assert_parent_child_write(old.family_id, old.child_id)` and `return old` (skipping the control-character and hourly-bound branches, which are insert-only). Alternatively revoke the DELETE grant and have routes/learning.ts delete with the service role, as child_profiles and safety_reports now do.
findings.leadDecision: Revoke the test_dates DELETE grant from authenticated and move that API delete to the service role (it already derives family and child from verified claims). That removes the last client DELETE in the guarded set.

findings.title: The core_identity regression that proved child_profiles' insert policy requires a session-bound adult unlock was replaced by an assertion that cannot fail, leaving 0860's "second layer" unverified
findings.mechanism: 0860 line 120 states: "The RLS policies child_profiles_member_insert / _member_update and safety_reports_parent_insert stay in place: they are the second layer if a column grant is ever restored." The test that used to prove the insert policy's content did so behaviourally (insert refused without a step-up, refused with a step-up on another auth session, accepted with the matching one, returning status 'draft'). The rewrite keeps only `expect(policies).toHaveLength(2)` and `for (const p of policies) expect(p.with_check ?? '').not.toBe('')`. Every INSERT/UPDATE policy in Postgres has a non-empty with_check expression, so that assertion holds for `with_check = true`. The adjacent `select app.has_recent_adult_unlock()` checks only that the helper function is session-bound, not that the policy calls it. Grepping supabase/tests for `child_profiles_member_insert` and `has_recent_adult_unlock` shows core_identity.test.ts:157/167/188 are the only hits, so nothing else pins the policy's content either.
findings.repro: In the probe DB the policy is `child_profiles_member_insert` WITH CHECK `(app.is_family_member(family_id) AND app.has_recent_adult_unlock() AND (status = 'draft'::text))`. Reduce it to `app.is_family_member(family_id)` (or to `true`) and the db suite still passes: the only assertions about it are the length-2 count and the non-empty-string check at line 169. The second layer 0860 relies on would then silently be gone — restoring an insert column grant on child_profiles later would let a parent create a profile with no step-up and with status 'active'.
findings.proof: Read supabase/tests/core_identity.test.ts:140-176 (the rewritten test) and `select policyname, with_check from pg_policies where tablename='child_profiles'` in pl_probe860, which printed the with_check quoted above. `grep -rn "child_profiles_member_insert|has_recent_adult_unlock" supabase/tests/*.ts` returned only core_identity.test.ts:157, :167, :188 — no other test constrains the policy body.
findings.suggestedFix: Assert the policy body, e.g. `expect(insertPolicy.with_check).toMatch(/has_recent_adult_unlock/)` and `/status = 'draft'/`, or keep a behavioural proof by re-granting the insert column privilege inside a rolled-back superuser transaction and re-running the three step-up cases against the policy.
findings.leadDecision: Restore equivalent coverage for the child_profiles insert policy: assert the grant is gone AND that the policy predicate still requires a session-bound adult unlock (a service-role probe of the policy, or an explicit pg_policies assertion). Never leave a weaker assertion in place of a behavioural one.
